entries.title: Creature Might
entries.summary: Might Score gives a supernatural creature Magic Resistance, fuels its powers through the Might Pool and sets Penetration; the Pool normally refreshes over a day.
quotes: A creature that hasn't used any powers recently has a Might Pool equal to its Might Score.
Might Pools almost always refresh to the creature's Might Score over the course of a day.
CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier

entries.title: Creature Powers
entries.summary: Creature powers have no levels and instead cost Might points, with a standard format, a Penetration formula based on Might and cost, and a dispelling level equal to Might.
quotes: Power Name, X points, Init Y, Form: Description.
CREATURE POWER PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost of the power) + Penetration Bonus
CREATURE POWER LEVEL FOR DISPELLING: Creature's Might Score

entries.title: Creature Format
entries.summary: Line-by-line explanation of a creature's stat block (Might, Characteristics with Cunning, Size, Confidence, Fatigue and Wound Penalty notation, Abilities, Powers, Vis).
quotes: Size 0 is the same size (volume, and thus normally roughly mass) as an adult human being.
An increase or decrease of three points of Size is approximately equivalent to a factor of ten change in size.

entries.title: Size Examples
entries.summary: Table of Size values with approximate heights, weights and example creatures, and the rule of thumb that each Size category roughly doubles weight.
quotes: Each Size category is approximately twice as heavy as the previous size category.

entries.title: Creating Creatures
entries.summary: Advice for storyguides designing creatures: start from a concept and role, then choose Might, combat statistics and power costs to suit the intended challenge.
quotes: A Might Score of 20 indicates that starting magi will have a lot of trouble affecting the creature with magic.

entries.title: Swallow Whole (new Mundane Quality)
entries.summary: The scorpion fish stat block introduces a reusable Swallow Whole Quality with rules for escaping, suffocation, stomach acid damage and bracing against immersion.
quotes: The scorpaena can swallow whole any creature of Size 0 or smaller.
The fish cannot swallow a second creature until the previous one has reached the stomach.

entries.title: Angelic Powers
entries.summary: The powers every angel possesses: Angelic Mantle to take a material form, Enfolding to protect a soul or body from all harm briefly, and Envisioning to deliver Divine messages in dreams or waking visions.
quotes: All angels possess the following powers:
An angel may also Enfold a person's body (costing 10 Might points)

entries.title: Divine Beings
entries.summary: Defines a divine being as any creature with Divine Might and describes where such beings live and how they interact with humans.

entries.title: What Are Angels?
entries.summary: Defines angels as the spiritual inhabitants of Heaven with Divine Might, their membership of a single Choir, and where each Choir tends to be found.

entries.title: Angelic Choirs
entries.summary: Lists the three Hierarchies and nine Choirs of angels, from most to least exalted.

entries.title: Angelic Traits (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the shared traits all angels have and the extra traits each Hierarchy grants, and how Seferiel from the core book fits.

entries.title: Angelic Traits
entries.summary: The baseline statistics every angel shares: minimum Divine Might, a fixed Personality Trait, the ability to be a conduit for a miracle and obedience to divine law.
quotes: All angels possess the Personality Trait "Love of God" +5.

entries.title: Angelic Characteristics
entries.summary: How to set an angel's Characteristics: non-physical ones derive from Divine Might, physical ones from a point-buy for its Mantle.
quotes: Angels with 1-10 Divine Might have a +1 in all non-physical Characteristics; angels with 11-20 Divine Might have +2 in all non-physical Characteristics, and so on.

entries.title: Angelic Free Will
entries.summary: Guidance on how angels act freely but always in accord with God's will, and notes that they can be wounded or destroyed.

entries.title: Angelic Senses
entries.summary: Angels perceive directly rather than through senses, so their perception cannot be targeted by spells.

entries.title: Angelic Movement
entries.summary: Angels move instantaneously, though in a Mantle they usually move naturally.

entries.title: Angelic Language
entries.summary: Angels communicate by illumination, which has a Penetration of zero, so they often speak human languages to magi.
quotes: This speech has a Penetration of zero (modified by any Penetration Ability the angel may have)

entries.title: Angelic True Names
entries.summary: True Names of angels act as arcane connections and aid Penetration for anyone who learns them.
quotes: True Names act as indefinite Arcane Connections, and grant a +5 multiplier bonus to a caster's Penetration multiplier.

entries.title: Angels and Magic
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic can affect angels in Mantle or in spiritual form, their immunities, and how they can be destroyed.
quotes: angels can be destroyed permanently by reducing their Divine Might to a negative value.

entries.title: Angels, Auras, and Regiones
entries.summary: What angels automatically know about auras, how they enter regiones, and the Second Sight rating they use to find non-Divine regiones.
quotes: All angels are considered to have a Second Sight Ability score equal to their Divine Might ÷ 5 for the purposes of finding non-Divine regiones.

entries.title: Seraphim (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Seraphim.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 35
with the level of the effect determined by the number of Might Points spent multiplied by 10

entries.title: Cherubim (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Cherubim.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 25

entries.title: Thrones (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Thrones.
quotes: The Holy Influence Total of a Throne using this power is equal to his Divine Might ÷ 2

entries.title: Dominations (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Dominations.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 10

entries.title: Authorities (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Authorities, including how Might reflects an Authority's office.
quotes: An Authority responsible for a flower may have Divine Might 5, while an Authority responsible for a thunder storm or a mountain has a Might of 15 or 20.

entries.title: Potentates (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Potentates.
quotes: The cost of the power is equal to the cost of the diabolical power it is opposing.

entries.title: Principalities (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Principalities, including the Might cost scaled to the size of the area protected.
quotes: A family costs 5 Might points, a hamlet or village costs 10, a town or city costs 15, a duchy costs 20, a kingdom or nation costs 30, and an empire, such as Byzantium or the Islamic Caliphate, costs 40 points.

entries.title: Archangels (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Archangels.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 50
doing +40 damage to all non-Divine beings (doubled against creatures with Infernal Might), and stripping non-Divine beings of 10 points of Might

entries.title: Angels (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by the lowest Choir of angels.
quotes: the angel may modify by 3 (plus or minus) any Personality Trait roll that could result in the target acting virtuously or piously

entries.title: Portraying Angels
entries.summary: Advice on playing angels as near-perfect but fallible beings, and on how they appear in an Envisioning or in a disguised Mantle.
quotes: Angels can make mistakes, over- or under-estimate someone, and be outwitted or fooled.

entries.title: Beasts in Combat
entries.summary: Beasts can use most human combat options, usually fight as untrained groups, and may use only one natural weapon per round, the best listed first.
quotes: Regardless of how many weapons a beast has, it may only attack with one weapon in a given round.

entries.title: Creating Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces the step-by-step method for building statistics for any mundane beast, for example a shapechanger's animal form.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Beasts are sorted into four categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts), which drive later steps.
quotes: There are four categories of beasts: Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 2: Characteristics
entries.summary: Beasts use Cunning instead of Intelligence, spend characteristic points only on the four physical Characteristics, then adjust Strength and Quickness for Size; mental Characteristics come from the beast's type.
quotes: Unlike human characters, animals only spend points on their four physical characteristics (Stamina, Strength, Dexterity and Quickness).
Add twice the Size to Strength
Subtract Size from Quickness

entries.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication for each beast type.

versions.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication by beast type, and how Increased Characteristics applies to beasts.

entries.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of typical Size and physical Characteristics for common kinds of animal, as starting points for new beasts.

versions.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of sample physical Characteristics for common creature types, with the rule for applying Size adjustments after spending points.
quotes: add twice the Size to Strength and subtract the Size from Quickness

entries.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
entries.summary: How to scale a creature larger or smaller than average, such as after a Muto Animal spell, by adjusting Strength, Quickness and wound ranges per Size point.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense totals), and decrease the damage range for each wound level by 1 (minimum of 1)

versions.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
versions.summary: How to adjust Strength, Quickness and wound ranges for creatures bigger or smaller than their type's norm, including the effect of Muto Animal size spells.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage Total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense Totals)

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 3: Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Species Virtues and Flaws come free to all members of a species and are not balanced for game purposes, while exceptional individuals need balanced individual Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: It is recommended that a species have at least one point of Flaws for every three points of Virtues.

entries.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts
entries.summary: Lists Virtues and Flaws appropriate to beasts and a note that Improved Characteristics grants more characteristic points to larger creatures.
quotes: A creature of Size +1 or smaller gets 3 characteristic points from this Virtue as normal, a creature of Size +2 gets 6 characteristic points, a creature of size +3 gets 9 characteristic points, and so on.

alsoIn.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 4: Basic Abilities
entries.summary: Table of the Abilities every creature of each type has, plus rules that animals with Cunning cannot gain experience or learn new Abilities as adults except through an Animal Handling teacher.
quotes: Animals (at least, those with Cunning rather than Intelligence) cannot acquire experience points to improve their Abilities once they have reached adulthood, nor can they learn new Abilities.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 5: Qualities
entries.summary: Catalog of creature Qualities (such as Ambush Predator, Constriction, Grapple, Overrun, Swallow Whole, Tough Hide and Venomous) that adjust characteristics, Abilities, Protection and special attacks, with how extra Fatigue levels are granted.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level, two extra grant another Winded Level and another Weary Level, etc.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 6: Combat Statistics
entries.summary: A beast's combat totals are calculated as normal using the Natural Weapons Table.
quotes: Combat Statistics are calculated as normal (page 393), using the Natural Weapons Table.

entries.title: Natural Weapons Table
entries.summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers for natural weapons such as teeth, claws, horns and hooves.
quotes: All natural weapons use the Brawl Ability.

entries.title: Aging of Animals
entries.summary: Adjusts the age at which aging starts, the age modifier and the number of aging rolls per year for an animal from its average lifespan relative to a human's.
quotes: Thus a creature with an average lifespan of 10 years has a modifier of (50/10) or five.

entries.title: Appendix: Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces a step-by-step system for generating statistics for heartbeasts, familiars and other mundane creatures.

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Defines the four beast categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts, Clawed Beasts) and how Size steps relate to weight, with the bird adjustment.
quotes: A 1-point difference in Size doubles the weight

entries.title: Size Examples (animals)
entries.summary: Table of example animals at each Size value from -15 to +9.

entries.title: Ferocity (beast Virtue)
entries.summary: A beast-only Minor Virtue giving confidence points that can be used only in situations that trigger the animal's natural ferocity.
quotes: take 3 confidence Points and a confidence Score of 1

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 5: Qualities
entries.summary: A list of animal Qualities (Aggressive, Camouflage, Fast Runner, Grapple, Venomous and so on) that adjust Characteristics, grant Abilities or modify combat, plus how extra Fatigue levels are handled.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level
Add +3 to all rolls involving running.

entries.title: Animal Creation Example: Bear
entries.summary: Worked example of the mundane beast design procedure, building a bear step by step and ending with a full stat block.

entries.title: Beast Statistics
entries.summary: Rules for mundane beast statistics: Characteristics outside the human range need no Virtue, Cunning replaces Intelligence, beasts cannot learn new Abilities without training, and they have no Might or vis.
quotes: Beasts do not need a Virtue or Flaw to have Characteristics outside the normal human range of –3 to +3.

entries.title: Modifying Beast Sizes
entries.summary: How to change a beast's Size by adjusting Strength and Quickness per point of Size, then updating combat statistics.
quotes: add 2 points of Strength and subtract one point of Quickness for each point of Size added

entries.title: Training Creatures (Overview)
entries.summary: Introduces taming of animals with a Cunning characteristic, by magi, magical characters or mundane handlers, followed by further training in tricks.

entries.title: Taming Animals
entries.summary: Taming is a seasonal activity accumulating points over consecutive seasons until they exceed the creature's Might; the tamer may split points among creatures of one species up to a limit set by Animal Handling.
quotes: REQUIRED POINTS TO TAME A CREATURE: Might of the Creature, Minimum 1

entries.title: Taming Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Sidebar giving mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and noting that taming is a social activity so The Gift penalties apply.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score

versions.title: Taming Mundane Beasts
versions.summary: Gives mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and notes that Gift penalties apply because taming is social.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 times Confidence Score

entries.title: A Hermetic Tamer
entries.summary: A magus tames an animal as a laboratory activity using a Rego (Form) Lab Total, producing a Lab Text that can later be reused to tame another creature of the same species.
quotes: TAMING POINTS ACCUMULATED EACH SEASON: Re(Fo) Lab Total – Creature's Might

entries.title: Hermetic Bonuses to Taming Lab Total
entries.summary: List of bonuses added to a Hermetic taming Lab Total: Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Experimentation and similar Lab Texts.
quotes: Animal Handling Ability Score
Animal Ken Ability Score

entries.title: A Mundane Trainer
entries.summary: Taming points per season for a mundane handler, who can usually only tame beasts with a small Magic Might.
quotes: Int + Animal Handling + Animal Ken – Creature's Might

entries.title: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
entries.summary: Who may command a tamed animal, and that a tamed animal is not considered to be under a continuing mystical effect.

entries.title: Loyalty
entries.summary: A tamed creature gains a Loyal Personality Trait towards its tamer; Loyalty Tests and extra seasons of training can raise or transfer that loyalty.
quotes: LOYALTY TEST: Loyal Personality Trait + stress die vs Ease Factor

entries.title: Training Animal Abilities
entries.summary: A character with Animal Handling can train a tamed animal's existing Abilities with the standard training rules, and the troupe may allow new Abilities subject to a Loyalty test.
quotes: make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Trained Groups of Animals
entries.summary: A handler may lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling in place of Leadership, with exceptions to the usual Combat Score matching.
quotes: The character's Animal Handling Ability score is used instead of his Leadership Ability score

entries.title: Commanding a Creature
entries.summary: Roll to command a tamed beast against an Ease Factor set by how unusual, frightening or dangerous the task is, with Loyalty tests required for the most extreme tasks.
quotes: COMMAND BEAST: Presence + Animal Handling (or Ride or Magic Lore) + stress die vs Ease Factor

entries.title: Animal Training and Commanding Beasts
entries.summary: A trainer spends seasons building training points against an animal's Might, and once the animal is trained the trainer rolls to have it obey commands of varying difficulty. The same rules serve riders training mounts, who may use Ride in place of Animal Handling.
quotes: This total is the character's Intelligence + Animal Handling – Creature's Might.
a mundane animal is considered to have a Might score of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score
Presence + Animal Handling + stress die vs. a variable Ease Factor

entries.title: Training Animals (Training Points)
entries.summary: Seasonal procedure for taming a mundane animal: a trainer accumulates training points each season until they equal the animal's Might, with a penalty for The Gift; also notes how Might is derived for mundane animals and that training is individual-specific.
quotes: Intelligence + Animal Handling + Animal Ken – Creature's Might – Gift Penalty
Mundane Animal Might = 1 + (2 x Confidence Score)

entries.title: Taming Creatures
entries.summary: A seasonal activity in which a character accumulates taming points from Intelligence + Animal Handling until a threshold based on the creature's Confidence is exceeded, plus rules for commanding tamed animals, building or transferring their Loyalty, and training their Abilities.
quotes: The taming is complete when the accumulated total of points exceeds a total equal to 1 + (2 x the creature's Confidence Score).
Each additional season of training increases the Loyal Personality Trait by +1, to a maximum of +3.
make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Animal Handling (magical beings)
entries.summary: Extends the Animal Handling Ability to managing and training elementals, animate trees, animal spirits and other beings with Cunning instead of Intelligence.
quotes: you can apply the same principles when interacting with other beings that have Cunning instead of Intelligence

entries.title: Social Abilities and Magical Beings
entries.summary: Summarizes which social Abilities apply to magical beings: most work with any intelligent being, Folk Ken only covers humans and human-like beings, and Magic Lore substitutes for it when judging magical beings' motives.
quotes: Magic Lore: This may be used like Folk Ken when attempting to understand the motivations and personality of magical beings.

entries.title: Spirit types: airy spirits, genii loci and daimons
entries.summary: Short definitions distinguishing airy spirits, the more powerful genii loci that embody a place, and daimons that act in the world only through replaceable aspects.
quotes: More powerful are the genii loci or spirits of place

entries.title: Animating Corpses with Magic
entries.summary: How a corpse animated by a Rego Corpus spell, demonic possession or a Magic spirit is statted: no fatigue, no powers of its own, and a Might score only when a spirit's power animates it.
quotes: Its Brawl skill is nominally 3, though as an optional rule the troupe may wish to assign a Brawl score equal to the caster's Finesse.
Regardless of how the corpse is animated, its unarmed attacks can be blocked by Magic Resistance.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.75

entries.title: The Magic of the Titanoi (Commanding Spirits and Daimons)
entries.summary: Explains how Form and Mentem spells command spirits, and how a Daimon can send an Aspect to a magus who forms a pact with it through a ritual spell.
quotes: Spells of a specific Form can command any spirit tied to that Form, for example, Ignem can command any fiery spirit.

entries.title: Laying Ghosts and Revenants the Mundane Way
entries.summary: Non-magical methods of putting restless ghosts and vengeful revenants to rest, such as completing unfinished tasks, giving a proper burial, or exhuming, beheading and blessing the grave of a revenant.

entries.title: Corrupt Beasts
entries.summary: How animals become corrupt (demonic influence, birth, Infernal auras or diabolists) and how to build one: start from a mundane beast, apply the compulsory Corrupted Beast Flaw and balance it with Virtues and Flaws from a restricted list.
quotes: To create the game statistics of a Corrupt Beast, start with the statistics of a mundane beast, and apply the Corrupted Beast Flaw.
The corpse of a corrupted beast typically contains one pawn of vis for each five points of Might it possessed.

entries.title: Virtues & Flaws for Corrupted Beasts
entries.summary: Lists the compulsory Flaw, the Virtues and the optional Flaws that a corrupted beast may be built from.
quotes: Optional Flaws: Horrifying Appearance, Demonic Weakness, Lesser Malediction

entries.title: How Big is a Giant?
entries.summary: A table of approximate height and weight for each Size, noting that Size determines height and weight rather than the reverse.
quotes: a character's height and weight are determined by his Size Characteristic, not the other way round

entries.title: Giants in Combat
entries.summary: An optional rule of thumb giving giants a defensive bonus against scuffling, grappling and disarming by smaller opponents, and notes on Corpus spells against giants.
quotes: a giant gains a special defensive bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's

entries.title: True Names and Synthemata
entries.requires: Knowledge of a being's True Name or synthemata (theurgy)
entries.summary: Explains True Names, which act as indefinite-duration Arcane Connections to spirits and are learned as spell-like abilities with experience points, and synthemata, the signs and passwords that every being with Might has and that theurgic magic uses to command it.
quotes: Each True Name is a spelllike ability recorded as "True Name of (Being)" on the character sheet, and costs 5 experience points to learn.
Knowing the True Name of a creature adds 5 to all lab totals to research synthemata for that same being.
A True Name is an Arcane Connection of indefinite duration

alsoIn.title: Arcane Connections, True Names, and Synthemata (Spirits)

entries.title: True Names
entries.summary: True Names are the only Arcane Connection to a spirit that has no body; characters buy each with experience in Infernal Lore, and a known True Name aids penetration and synthemata research.
quotes: a +5 bonus to the Penetration Multiplier when penetrating an Infernal creature's Magic Resistance
Each True Name costs 5 experience points

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 9: Theurgy

entries.title: Demons and Magic
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic interacts with demons: deceptions and Infernal Might are invisible to truth-revealing spells, Second Sight is harder against them, they can be warded and attacked with Vim, and summoning them is forbidden by the Oath of Hermes.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot pierce any deception produced by a demon
this Ease Factor is increased by the magnitude of their Might.
a demon that is reduced to an Infernal Might of zero is destroyed, leaving behind no corpse (and thus no vis)

entries.title: Using Abilities On Faeries
entries.summary: Summarises how the common Abilities (Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Folk Ken, Faerie Lore, Language, Teaching and social Abilities) apply to faeries.
quotes: Any Faerie with a score in Faerie Speech can understand any language.
Faeries cannot be taught, since they do not learn by doing.

entries.title: Antagonists for grog stories
entries.summary: Guidance on choosing antagonists for grog-only stories, noting that grogs lack Magic Resistance so even weak supernatural powers threaten them, how a Brave roll can decide whether a band stands against a fear power, and how to keep a trained group from defeating the antagonist too early.
quotes: Grogs have no Magic Resistance at all

entries.title: The Types of Horses
entries.summary: Explains how the horse templates (destrier, courser or rouncey, palfrey or jennet, draught horse and working pony) can be individualized, then gives each template's statistics, uses, typical price and where the best animals come from.
quotes: Horse templates typical of each type are provided that the storyguide can modify to individualize horses available at market or presented as gifts.
Owning such a beast is worth at least a single experience point in Reputation: Prudhomme.
A courser usually costs around 10 to 20 pounds

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.40

entries.title: Creatures of Faerie: Roles and Pretenses
entries.summary: General rules for faeries: they are bound to story roles they cannot break, their physical attacks ignore Magic Resistance, and they have Pretenses rather than Abilities, which a skilled observer may detect with a Perception + Awareness roll.
quotes: Despite this, their physical attacks are not blocked by Magic Resistance, including the Parma Magica.
Faeries have Pretenses instead of Abilities.
may make a Perception + Awareness roll against an Ease Factor of 12

entries.title: Faerie Virtues and Flaws (Cognizance, Wards, Faerie Sight and Speech)
entries.summary: Explains the faerie-specific traits used to build faeries: regeneration without fatigue, degrees of Cognizance, Faerie Sight, Faerie Speech, and Traditional and Sovereign Wards that harm or exclude a faerie.
quotes: Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
Direct contact with a sovereign ward destroys the body of a faerie, removing it from the scenario.
The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.

versions.title: Faerie Virtues and Flaws
versions.summary: Explains that a Supernatural Virtue can be designated as having a Faerie origin, which gives it the Faerie bonuses on the Realm Interaction Table and spares the character Warping from living in a Faerie aura; notes Benediction and Malediction as typical faerie gifts and curses.
quotes: characters with a Faerie Virtue or Flaw do not gain Warping from living in a Faerie aura.
related: ArM5 pp.54-55 Greater and Lesser Malediction

entries.title: Cognizance: Incognizant, Narrow and High
entries.summary: Classifies faeries by how well they understand their own need for human vitality (incognizant, narrowly cognizant, highly cognizant), which governs their memory, pain, planning and ability to change themselves.
quotes: All faeries require human vitality, and seek it instinctively.

related.text: Chapter 3: Faerie Characters, Cognizance Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Glamour: Rules Instead of a Soul
entries.summary: Describes glamour as the set of rules tied to a faerie's role; a faerie cannot break them and fades if it stops fulfilling its role, and it grows stronger by taking part in stories.
quotes: Faeries cannot break their glamour.

entries.title: Faerie Bodies and Spiritual Anchors
entries.summary: A faerie builds its body from incidental matter around a spiritual anchor; the anchor holds the faerie's vis and lets it rebuild after its body is destroyed, and pain depends on cognizance.
quotes: Incognizant faeries feel pain when their bodies are damaged, narrowly cognizant faeries must appear to, and highly cognizant faeries suffer pain only if they wish to.
The spiritual anchor, filled with glamour, is the vis that magi hunt so earnestly.

entries.title: Faerie Ownership and Stolen Goods
entries.summary: Items a faerie owns are part of its glamour and revert to incidental matter, with any vis vanishing, if taken against its will; its possessions and mortal belongings with Arcane Connections matter to faeries.
quotes: All of a faerie's possessions, if generated from glamour, are Arcane Connections to the faerie until it changes its role.

entries.title: Faerie Taboos
entries.summary: Each faerie has mandatory and forbidden actions; a human who breaks one offends the faerie and owes redress, and may take this as the origin of a Story Flaw.
quotes: A human breaking the taboos of a faerie offends it, and owes it redress.

entries.title: Pretenses and Noticing Them
entries.summary: Faeries mimic human Abilities with Pretenses, which cost no Might and need no Concentration; masters of the imitated Ability can notice the deception with a Perception + Awareness check against a stated difficulty.
quotes: Pretenses do not cost Might, and faeries use them without Concentration
This requires a Perception + Awareness check of 12 – the Ability score the faerie is pretending to have.

related.text: Chapter 3: Faerie Characters, Pretense: Faerie Abilities

entries.title: No Numerical System for Vitality
entries.summary: Sidebar stating that the game tracks no points of vitality: faeries do not spend it to survive or advance, they simply always want more.
quotes: There is no numerical system for vitality.

entries.title: Vitality: How Faeries Feed
entries.summary: Describes the ways faeries harvest human vitality (roused emotion, art, offerings, theft, border crossings, blood and flesh, violence), which the storyguide uses to decide what a faerie wants and does.

entries.title: Designing Faerie Characters: Sequence of Choices
entries.summary: Overview of the order of decisions for creating a faerie: player or non-player, power level, Might, physical form, cognizance, role, powers and vulnerabilities.
quotes: Faeries are designed through a series of choices.

entries.title: Faerie Characters: PC or NPC
entries.summary: Non-player faeries may be more powerful than new player characters and need not balance Virtues and Flaws; the bestiary uses these rules as examples but troupes may design more informally.
quotes: Non-player characters do not need to balance their Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Faerie Level of Power
entries.summary: A player faerie should be about as powerful as a companion or magus, and the troupe should agree on the design so that it does not reduce others' enjoyment.
quotes: approximately as powerful as a companion or magus

entries.title: Faerie Virtues, Flaws and Pretense Points
entries.summary: A player faerie replacing a companion or magus gets a limited allotment of Virtues balanced by Flaws, and a pool of Pretense points set by the average magus age; inherent Abilities of the physical form must be bought first.
quotes: 1 free, then up to 20 points of Virtues paid for with Flaws at 2 Virtues per Flaw.
(average age of magus player characters – 5) + 120 points
which gives 360 points of Pretences

entries.title: Required Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
entries.summary: Every faerie character needs a Might score, physical form, level of cognizance, Social Interaction Virtue and a taboo; innate powers can be traded away as Flaws.
quotes: A character must have a Might score, a physical form, a level of cognizance, a Social Interaction Virtue, and a taboo.

entries.title: Faerie Might Score and Might Points
entries.summary: Sets a starting Might score for player faeries, gives innate Magic Resistance equal to Might, and explains that Might Points are spent on powers and recover steadily over a day; notes that Might varies widely with role.
quotes: Player characters begin with a Faerie Might score of 5
Faerie Might gives the character innate Magic Resistance equal to its Might Score.
Faeries have Might Points equal in number to their Might score, which they spend to activate their powers.

entries.title: Quick Start Guideline (Faerie Characters)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving a fast recipe for a companion-level faerie: a stated Might, Characteristics and Pretence points, a short list of Virtues, free choices and a Traditional Ward Flaw.
quotes: has a Faerie Might of 10
360 Points of Pretences: Spend them exactly like Ability points.

entries.title: Faerie Physical Form: Ageing and Fatigue
entries.summary: Explains what a faerie body is and its advantages: no ageing or Decrepitude unless a Flaw says otherwise, no Fatigue, and great difficulty in dying.
quotes: Faeries cannot age or suffer Decrepitude unless they have a Flaw.

entries.title: Equipment Without Encumbrance
entries.summary: A faerie carries traditional props of its role without Encumbrance and can reconstitute a lost prop for no Might in a round.
quotes: Reconstituting a prop costs no Might, and requires a single round.

entries.title: Faerie Regeneration and Rebuilding a Body
entries.summary: Faeries heal by cognizance level, and a faerie killed before humans rebuilds a body in a time set by its Might and the local aura; memory and role changes after rebuilding depend on cognizance.
quotes: The time taken to regenerate equals the faster of the Faerie Might Score in months or Faerie Might Score / Aura (as modified by the Realm Interaction Table) in months.

entries.title: Scale of Typical Might Scores
entries.summary: Sidebar table giving descriptive Might bands from ordinary creatures to earth-shaking figures with example bestiary faeries at each level.
quotes: | 1–10 | An ordinary creature of a realm. |

entries.title: Permanent Death of Faeries
entries.summary: Lists what kills a faerie permanently: destroyed Might Score, miracles, Infernal agents, use of the vis in its anchor, and antithetical things for incognizant faeries with a Sovereign Ward.
quotes: A faerie whose Might Score is destroyed dies permanently.

entries.title: Magic Resistance Against Faeries
entries.summary: Faerie bodies and props are not blocked by Parma Magica or other Magic Resistance, though wards targeting the faerie's material or spiritual nature work, and powers with a Might cost and a Range beyond Personal are generally resisted.
quotes: Faerie bodies, and the other props created by the same process, are not, however, blocked by the Parma Magica or other forms of Magic Resistance.
The powers of faeries that have Might costs and ranges greater than Personal are, in most cases, opposed by Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Faerie Human and Animal Forms
entries.summary: How to build Characteristics for humanoid and animal-form faeries, and how animal-form player faeries swap Cunning for Intelligence as a free Virtue.
quotes: A humanoid faerie has 7 points with which to buy Characteristics
This is a Free Virtue.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, Book of Mundane Animals
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Hybrid Forms and Natural Weapons
entries.summary: Hybrid forms are human forms with animal elements that are cosmetic or Minor Virtues; faeries' natural weapons use Brawl and a table of Init, Atk, Dfn and Dmg values and need no Virtue.
quotes: This uses the Brawl Ability and the statistics on the following table.
Having natural weapons does not, in itself, require a Virtue.

entries.title: Glamorous, Immaterial Forms
entries.summary: Immaterial faeries are invisible and pass through solid objects but must take on matter to move things; design them as the physical body they don, with the Intangible Flesh Flaw.
quotes: Immaterial faeries are invisible to those without magical aid, and can pass through solid objects.

entries.title: Faerie Size
entries.summary: Humanoid faeries choose a Size with required Strength and Quickness adjustments; extreme sizes need troupe scrutiny, and nonhuman characters adjust Characteristics only if they deviate more than one from their base Size.
quotes: Characters outside the range of Size +2 to –3 are difficult to accommodate in sagas, and should be carefully scrutinized by the Troupe.
Characters deviating from their base size by 1 do not change Characteristics, but those deviating by more than 1 are adjusted as indicated by the table above.

entries.title: What Do Size Scores Represent?
entries.summary: Reference table of Size scores from tiny to huge with height, weight, comparison creature and the wound-penalty ranges for each Size.
quotes: | Size | Height | Weight | Comparison | Wound Penalties |

entries.title: Faerie Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Faeries take Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws that cover only dealings with humans and replace Social Status Virtues; with other faeries a player faerie is treated as a representative of its human companions.
quotes: govern only their interaction with humans and replace Social Status Virtues

entries.title: Faerie Cognizance in Character Design
entries.summary: A faerie's cognizance shapes its goals and limits how it can develop new powers: low-cognizance faeries do not consciously improve, middling ones transform predictably, and highly cognizant ones can change roles between scenes.
quotes: Characters of low cognizance do not consciously attempt to improve their statistics during the saga.

entries.title: Unspecialized Role (Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities)
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling that faeries can have Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities without the Virtues humans need, though professionals quickly detect the fraud.
quotes: Faeries do not require the Virtues that allow characters to have Martial, Arcane, or Academic Abilities to have Pretenses for them.

entries.title: Faerie Taboos: Traditional and Sovereign Wards
entries.summary: Faerie taboos are built from Ward Flaws: a Traditional Ward bars touching the ward, stops Might regeneration and burns the faerie as a damage source, while a Sovereign Ward bars harming the protected person and destroys the faerie's body on touch.
quotes: The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.
Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
the faerie may not harm a person or thing that is defended by the ward

entries.title: Folk Charms (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A faerie with this taboo cannot face folk charms deliberately used against it, whatever the culture; personal charms precious to a human also serve and are Arcane Connections to that human.
quotes: A character with this taboo cannot face folk charms, deliberately used, from any culture

entries.title: Herbs (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: The herbs that repel a faerie depend on its role and the herb's underlying symbolism; identifying the right herb needs Faerie Lore or the ability to read the faerie's glamour.
quotes: The herbs that repel a faerie are based on that faerie's role, so the faerie is unable to vary them, except by changing roles.

entries.title: Iron (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Iron is a common faerie ward, and some faeries refuse to deal with those carrying it, while miners, crafters and urban faeries are often comfortable with it.
quotes: Some faeries refuse to negotiate with humans who carry iron, even if they will not suffer from contact with it

entries.title: Names (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A character who knows the name of a faerie with this taboo can force it to leave him alone, so powerful faeries use titles and roles instead.
quotes: If a faerie has this taboo, and a character knows its name, the character can force the faerie to leave it alone.

entries.title: Payment or Thanks (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Some faeries must leave human service once paid or thanked, either because the relationship is balanced or their story is complete, and a few then turn on their former employers.
quotes: Some faeries must leave human service if paid or thanked.

entries.title: Places (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Place-based taboos must seriously inconvenience the faerie, for example foreign earth acting as a Traditional Ward, and a Sovereign Ward tying a faerie to its home makes it unsuitable for most player characters.
quotes: Flaws based on places must seriously inconvenience the character.
Characters tied to their home with a Sovereign Ward simply cannot leave, and are unsuitable as player characters in most sagas.

entries.title: Religious Symbols (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Faeries with this taboo flee symbols such as church bells; many powerful faeries also cannot enter the Dominion without God's invitation.
quotes: Many of the most powerful faeries cannot enter the Dominion, because God has not invited them in and they are unable to trespass.

entries.title: Focus Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie a themed, spontaneous-style power built from a pool of spell levels, with Might cost and Initiative set by the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The player receives 25 spell levels to spend on this power.
an initiative score of (the character's Quickness – the power's maximum magnitude)

entries.title: Greater Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers designed at character creation, with a reduced Might cost and Initiative penalty compared to Lesser Powers.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 50 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)

entries.title: Lesser Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers; cheaper to acquire than Greater Powers but each use costs more Might and is slower.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 25 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each effect's Might Point cost is equal to the magnitude of the effect.

entries.title: Personal Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie a single Personal-range spell-like power designed like a formulaic spell.
quotes: Personal powers must have Personal Range.

entries.title: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers
entries.summary: General rules for using faerie powers: spending Might for uses, Penetration, wound penalties, running out of Might, and powers across realm boundaries.
quotes: Faeries gain one use of a power each time they spend its cost in Might.
Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost) + Penetration bonus

entries.title: Intricacy Points
entries.summary: Intricacy points let a faerie make a power faster or cheaper in Might, and can be gained from unspent spell levels or the Improved Powers Virtue.
quotes: Every 5 unspent levels equal an intricacy point.

entries.title: Odd Targets and Durations
entries.summary: Allows faerie powers to use Merinita Ranges, Targets and Durations, and defines the Until Duration and dual Durations.
quotes: In this book it is treated as being equivalent to Year, but not requiring a Ritual.

entries.title: Faerie Power Virtue Comparison Table
entries.summary: Table comparing spell levels, effect type, Might cost and Initiative for each faerie power Virtue.
quotes: Qik – maximum magnitude

entries.title: Ritual Power
entries.summary: Major Virtue for ritual-level faerie effects, which cost Might Score as well as Might points whenever they are used.
quotes: All Ritual Powers are at least Level 20, regardless of the actual level of the effect
The Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2).

entries.title: Improved Powers
entries.summary: Minor Virtue granting intricacy points to a faerie's powers, or optionally mastery-like abilities for them.
quotes: This Virtue gives the character 5 intricacy points to spend on any of its powers.

entries.title: Constant Powers
entries.summary: Rules for making a Greater, Lesser or Personal Power constant, triggering at every sunrise and sunset.
quotes: costs an additional magnitude

entries.title: Binding Oath
entries.summary: Ritual faerie power enforcing solemn oaths and contracts, warning and then penalising humans who break them.
quotes: Faeries cannot break their oaths

entries.title: Granting Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Ritual faerie powers that impose a Virtue or Flaw (blessing or curse) on a target, permanently at the cost of Might Score or temporarily at the cost of Might points.
quotes: The creature can decide to bestow the Virtue permanently or temporarily.

entries.title: Converting Greater Powers to Lesser Powers
entries.summary: Quick procedure to convert a Greater Power to a Lesser Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the power

entries.title: Greater and Lesser Faerie Powers
entries.summary: Explains how Lesser Powers compare with Greater Powers and how the powers listed in the book are presented, including the Initiative bonus.
quotes: each use costs twice as much Might as the equivalent Greater Power

entries.title: Craft Magical Trinket
entries.summary: Faerie power that creates a glamour object letting its holder use one Virtue once, at a Might cost depending on the Virtue's size.
quotes: A trinket costs 10 Might points if it invokes a Minor Virtue, and 15 points if it invokes a Major Virtue.

entries.title: Loosely Material
entries.summary: Power letting an immaterial faerie take on a physical body, whose Characteristics and Size are bought with Might points spent on activation.
quotes: For each Might point spent on this power, 5 characteristic points are available to spend on the four physical Characteristics of Strength, Stamina, Dexterity, and Quickness.
A faerie's material body can have any Size up to a maximum of its Presence unless it spends additional Might points on Size.

entries.title: Powers of Transformation
entries.summary: Advice on which faerie power Virtue to use when designing transformation powers, depending on whether specific or varied substances are involved.
quotes: then that is best designed as a Greater Power

entries.title: Focus Powers
entries.summary: Intro to Focus Powers: broad themed effects whose Might cost and Initiative follow the magnitude produced, to be agreed with the troupe.
quotes: Each use of a focus power has a Might Point cost equal to the magnitude of the effect

entries.title: Power Design: An Example
entries.summary: Worked example of designing faerie powers from Hermetic spells, choosing between Personal, Greater, Lesser and Focus Powers and spending intricacy points.
quotes: Personal powers cost (magnitude/2) points, rounding up

entries.title: Pretense: Faerie Abilities
entries.summary: Explains that faeries use Pretenses in place of Abilities, and that few faeries can teach humans, especially those linked to the dead.
quotes: Some exceptional faeries are able to teach Abilities to humans.

entries.title: Faerie Instructor and Faerie Trainer
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Instructor or Faerie Trainer
entries.summary: Virtues allowing a faerie to teach humans, either by trading stored Abilities or by training with conventional methods.
quotes: The faerie imparts the Ability by trading it for the Ability that the student currently has.

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretenses
entries.summary: Pretenses tied to a faerie's story role rather than a human Ability must be negotiated with the troupe.
quotes: These player-defined pretenses must be negotiated with the troupe.

entries.title: Resistance and Pretenses
entries.summary: Explains that Pretenses guide a faerie's own actions and so are not resisted by Parma Magica, unlike powers or tools aimed at a magus.
quotes: they are not resisted by Parma Magica

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretense Example: Chivalrous Combat
entries.summary: Worked example of negotiating a broad player-defined Pretense with a built-in limitation.

entries.title: Increasing Pretense
entries.summary: How faeries gain Pretense experience by closely involving themselves in humans' stories each season, plus the Virtues and Flaws that change how often this occurs.
quotes: Faeries cannot gain experience from study, training, or practice
During character creation an ostentatious faerie has a Pretense multiplier of 25 instead of 15.

entries.title: Faerie Advancement Through Change
entries.summary: Overview of what a faerie needs to alter its role and gain powers: cognizance, stored Pretense points, and a creative human collaborator.
quotes: It requires the potential to change within its glamour, represented by the cognizance Virtues.

entries.title: Cognizance
entries.summary: Describes how incognizant, narrowly cognizant and highly cognizant faeries differ in their understanding of advancement.
quotes: Only highly cognizant faeries understand that they can use human vitality and creativity to tailor their roles in amusing ways.

entries.title: Vitality
entries.summary: Faeries store Pretense points as vitality for changing role, and can consume encased vis to lower the cost of change.
quotes: it reduces the Pretence Cost in the nearby table by 1 for every pawn of vis consumed, to a maximum of the faerie's Might score

entries.title: Creativity
entries.summary: Procedure and table by which a creative human collaborates to change a faerie's glamour, with Ease Factors, Pretense costs and the Virtue and Flaw changes they buy.
quotes: Lose a Virtue or Flaw and gain another of equal value
The Ease Factor should be reduced by 3 if the faerie’s role has drifted away from the folklore of the area

entries.title: Why Isn't My Faerie a Genius At Every Ability?
entries.summary: Explains why starting faerie characters lack great experience, including how and when faeries lose Pretenses.
quotes: Faeries often lose Pretenses.

entries.title: Faerie Monarchs
entries.summary: Design benchmark for how mighty a faerie ruler must be to threaten senior magi and why a court helps.
quotes: it requires a Faerie Might score of around 60, and the Penetration Pretense

entries.title: Faerie Blood: Origins and Inheritance
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood
entries.summary: Explains how humans come to have Faerie Blood (through faerie procreation, theft of fertility, or influence on a pregnancy or infant) and how the taint is inherited down the generations.
quotes: Faerie Blood manifests regardless of the number of generations between the first character to bear it and the current generation.

entries.title: Changelings
entries.summary: Introduces how faeries steal or exchange human infants, leaving behind a faerie child, an ancient faerie or a stock, and what results for the child who is retrieved or who is raised by faeries.

entries.title: Retrieved Changelings
entries.summary: Describes how parents can retrieve a stolen child by tricking the changeling faerie into revealing itself, and what a retrieved child tends to gain, such as Second Sight or Faerie Blood of the kidnappers' variety.

entries.title: Bear Island: Hunting Gegenees (faerie regeneration)
entries.summary: A slain Gegenes leaves its body and returns to its external-vis rock to craft a new body from glamor, so the supply of Gegenees to hunt is effectively unlimited and the corpse holds no vis.

entries.title: Faerie Cognizance and Pretenses
entries.summary: Explains that faeries are Incognizant, Narrowly Cognizant or Cognizant depending on how freely they can step outside their story role, and that they have Pretenses in place of Abilities. Pretenses are used exactly like Abilities in play.
quotes: Faeries have Pretenses instead of Abilities.
In play, use Pretenses exactly as Abilities

entries.title: Raising a Faerie's Might (Increased Might)
entries.summary: Quick way to make faeries tougher for powerful magi by giving them the Increased Might Virtue, in its Major or Minor form.
quotes: The Major Faerie Virtue Increased Might increases a faerie's Might Score by 15.

entries.title: Vitality Is No Longer Enough
entries.requires: Saga: the world after the Second Titanomachy
entries.summary: Explains how surviving faeries sustain themselves after the Titanomachy through a formal, knowing yearly exchange with humans, and how those who fail lose Might and Virtues over time.
quotes: Faeries incapable of forging or sustaining a formal bond with humans cannot maintain their glamour and lose one point of Might every year.

entries.title: Giants and their Mothers (Transylvanian giants)
entries.summary: Describes how Transylvanian giants differ from the stock stupid giant: they are refined, arm and armor themselves like knights, and can change Size and shape. Used when designing or running giant faeries.
quotes: many Transylvanian giants can change Size, ranging from Size +2 to +5, with some growing even larger

entries.title: Giants' Mothers
entries.summary: Explains the faerie role of the giant's mother, a sorceress who manages her son, pursues those who defeat him, and adopts a new son if she loses him. Also notes the hereditary hair growing under the tongue of those with giant blood.
quotes: A giant's mother is always a sorceress, and invariably smarter than her son.

entries.title: Faerie Horses
entries.summary: Describes the faerie horse's story role (rescued from a giant's mother's ranch, serves a hero, leaves before the final victory) and the limited foresight a highly cognizant faerie has about other faeries' roles.
quotes: He cannot see into the future, but because he is more cognizant than other participating faeries

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.62 Flight

entries.title: Vilas (White Ladies)
entries.summary: Introduces vilas as faerie women who play different roles in each community, to be built from a generic faerie woman and tailored to the role.
quotes: Storyguides designing vilas should use the statistics for a generic faerie woman, and then tailor them to the role that the particular vila plays.

entries.title: Generic Minor Vila (template and power-conversion notes)
entries.summary: Template for a weak generic vila usable as a grog-level antagonist or player character, with notes on buying powers as Greater or Lesser Powers, Personal Powers and a quick-play option for faerie power costs.
quotes: Troupes preferring speed over accuracy should double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the powers given here.

entries.title: Vila Wards (hair, offerings and External Vis)
entries.summary: Describes vila Wards: a strand of hair as a Sovereign Ward, hair as a Minor External Vis source that keeps the vila from truly dying, the Residual Power Virtue, and offerings used as Traditional Wards.
quotes: Vilas often have a Sovereign Ward Flaw for a strand of their own hair.
The hair of a vila is often a Minor External Vis source.

entries.title: Powers Found In Many Roles (vila powers)
entries.summary: Introduces the five groups of powers common to vilas regardless of role: Shapeshifter, Enthralling Voice, Blessing Dance, Cursing Dance and Spirit Away.

entries.title: Vila Shapeshifter Powers
entries.summary: Lists personal shapeshifting powers for vilas that turn them into animals, birds or fish, with Might cost and Initiative by Size and duration; transforming back to human costs the same as the inverse power.
quotes: Faeries retain the power of speech in animal form.
Transform into Human costs the same as the inverse power.

entries.title: Vila Enthralling Voice Powers
entries.summary: Mentem powers modelling a vila's voice: Allure, Enthralling Sound, Enthrallment, Guide, Kiss of Forgetfulness and Steal Judgment, with their costs, durations and the rolls used to resist them.
quotes: Grants a +3 bonus on all rolls that convince or impress others.
A Personality trait roll against an Ease Factor of 9 allows a character to ignore this effect.
Can be resisted with an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor of 6 for implausible lies.

entries.title: Vila Blessing Dance Powers
entries.summary: Powers a vila uses to grant magical gifts to mortals who dance with her or pass tests: Grant (Major or Minor Virtue) and Grant Puissance in an Ability.
quotes: For every added point spent, a group can be granted +1 on all rolls in a certain situation (combat or court, for example), or one character can be given +3 on a particular Total or roll

entries.title: Vila Cursing Dance Powers
entries.summary: Notes how cursed dances reuse the Enthralling Voice powers and adds Craft Magical Trinket, which makes a dancing circle a cursed magic item with a cost set by the severity of the Flaw.
quotes: This power, which makes the circle a kind of magic item, costs 10 points if the curse is a Minor Flaw, and 15 points if it is a Major Flaw.

entries.title: Spirit Away (vila power)
entries.summary: The power that lets faeries draw mortals into the Faerie realms, with a shortcut for troupes not using the full rules.
quotes: Troupes not using these rules should just assume the attempt succeeds when it suits the story.

entries.title: Role-Specific Vila Powers (customizing by role)
entries.summary: Explains how to build a vila for a story role, balancing added Virtues with Flaws for a player character, and how the Ostentatious and Pretentious Virtues give extra pretense points.
quotes: The first adds 10 times the average age of the PC magi points to the character's pool of pretense points. The second adds 5 times the average age of the PC magi points.

entries.title: Vila Role: Captured Wife
entries.summary: A vila who changes shape and is held by hiding her skin or feathers; the skin can be modeled mechanically as a Skinchanger prop, an External Vis Source or a Sovereign Ward.
quotes: The animal skins can be designed mechanically as the prop for the Skinchanger virtue, as External Vis Source, or as a Sovereign Ward

entries.title: Vila Role: Cloud or Storm Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for cloud and storm vilas: Flight, a Storms Focus power covering Hermetic weather spells up to a level cap, and Guide used to cause travelers to become lost.
quotes: The character has a range of weather-related powers, simulating all Hermetic weather spells of level 25 or less.

entries.title: Vila Role: Cursed Lover
entries.summary: A vila who unknowingly kills her mortal lovers through the Pine Away power, treated as a disease, or through a cursed trinket with a recurring accident motif.
quotes: Simulated as a major disease with an Ease Factor of 9 that causes a Light Wound.

entries.title: Vila Role: Huntress
entries.summary: Additions to the generic vila for a mounted archer, plus the Shake the Earth power which makes characters in 100 paces make a stress roll or fall, with listed modifiers.
quotes: Characters fall unless they make a Quickness – Encumbrance stress roll against an Ease Factor of 10, modified as follows: +2 standing still, +2 on solid stone, +0 moving slowly or on earth, –2 running, –6 on a narrow bridge.

entries.title: Vila Role: Temptress
entries.summary: Powers for a vila who steals young men into woods or waters: Allure, Illusory Home and Pine Away.

entries.title: Vila Role: Water Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for drowned-maiden vilas: Illusory Home and Kiss of the Mermaid, which lets the recipient breathe water until next stepping on dry land.

entries.title: Vila Role: Woodland Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for woodland vilas: Extend Glamor, Guide, a Manifestation Focus power covering Animal and Herbam spells within a level cap in the vila's glamour, and the Transform Victim powers.
quotes: Allows the faerie to simulate any Creo Animal, Rego Animal, Creo Herbam or Rego Herbam spell of level 25 or less in the area of its glamor.

entries.title: Vila Role: Wise Woman
entries.summary: A vila role that mimics a folk witch, with a Healing Focus power that simulates Hermetic healing spells up to a level cap, and a Prophecy power that is only a pretense of foresight.
quotes: Allows the faerie to simulate any Hermetic healing spell up to level 25.

entries.title: Bee King (Strong Faerie Blood variety)
entries.requires: Virtue: Strong Faerie Blood (Bee King variety)
entries.summary: Describes the special powers of a Bee King: commanding bees, speaking with hives, immunity to biting insects, and treating attacking bee swarms as an automatic damage effect rather than a melee group, along with the fixed lifespan drawback.
quotes: An attacking bee swarm is treated as an environmental effect, rather than an opposing mêlée group.

entries.title: Characters with Might Scores
entries.summary: Special rules for characters with a Might Score: no Virtues tied to another realm, magic resistance from several sources does not stack, immunity to Warping, and immunity to supernatural backlashes of their own realm.
quotes: Characters with a Might Score are immune to all Warping (see Warping and Non-Humans, page 389).
these totals do not stack

entries.title: Essential Traits
entries.requires: Creatures of the Magic Realm with essential traits
entries.summary: Describes essential traits, features of a Magic Realm creature's very nature (marked with an asterisk in its stats) that magic cannot force it to act against.
quotes: Magic cannot, therefore, make them act against those traits.
They are indicated with an asterisk in the character statistics

versions.title: Essential Traits
versions.summary: Personality Traits of magic characters become fixed Essential Traits that protect against effects forcing contrary behaviour, and Characteristic-specialty traits combine with Characteristics by a set method.
quotes: if the Characteristic is positive and the Trait is beneficial, use the greater of the two; if the Characteristic is negative and the Trait is detrimental, use the lesser of the two; otherwise, add the Trait to the Characteristic

entries.title: Bind Magical Creatures
entries.requires: Initiation: Bind Magical Creatures (Verditius Major Inner Mystery)
entries.summary: Lets a magus drain a magical creature's Magic Might as vis for a greater enchanted item, or permanently bind one of its powers to his Gift, with the Lab Total requirements, costs and permanent loss of Might; also covers Faerie Might and the risk of Warping.
quotes: For every point of Lab Total over the creature's Might score, the magus gains one pawn of vis that is usable toward the enchanted device.
the magus's Rego Vim Lab Total plus Hubris score must be equal to or exceed twice the creature's Magic Might.
Its Might is reduced by 5 times the Might cost necessary for the creature to use the power.

entries.title: Magic Characters: Might and Might Points
entries.summary: Overview of what Magic Might gives a magic character: Magic Resistance equal to Might, Might Points spent on powers and recovered over time, destruction when Might is reduced, freedom from deprivation (with penalties if it is ignored), and the ability to consume vis to restore Might Points.
quotes: Magic Might gives the character innate Magic Resistance equal to its Might Score
A magic character is destroyed if his Might Score is reduced to 0 or less.
Each pawn of vis from the same Form as the character’s Might Score will immediately replenish 5 Might Points, or 2 Might Points if this vis is associated with any other Art

entries.title: Magic Character Creation
entries.summary: Introduces the procedure for designing characters that begin play with Magic Might, such as familiars, ghostly warders or magical servants.

entries.title: Magic Character Creation Summary
entries.summary: Four-step summary of making a magic character: pick a concept (true form, Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Size), determine season and Abilities, set Magic Might and choose Qualities and Inferiorities, then add finishing touches.
quotes: Characteristics: 7 points assigned as in standard Detailed Character Creation (see ArM5 page 29), no Characteristic more than +3 or less than -3.
A spring character receives 120 experience points, a summer character receives 360, an autumn character receives 720, and a winter character receives 1200.

entries.title: Auras and Might Recovery
entries.summary: Resting in a Magic aura speeds recovery of Might Points; a subtotal from aura and Might Score gives the time to recover the whole pool, divided by Might Score for the per-point rate.
quotes: ENTIRE RECOVERY TIME: Subtotal = Aura - (Might Score / 5), then refer to chart
RECOVERY RATE: 1 Might Point per (Recovery Time / Might Score)

entries.title: Magic Character Concept
entries.summary: First step of making a magic character: choose its true form, assign base Characteristics, decide whether it is intelligent, take the Special Virtue for its type plus a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, other Virtues and Flaws, and set Size, which adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: you should begin with all eight scores at 0 and assign 7 points to them
adding two times Size to Strength, and subtracting Size from Quickness

entries.title: Magic Animal Characters
entries.summary: Rules for building a magic animal character from a mundane animal's stats: innate No Hands and Mute equivalents, required minimum Abilities, and a Size adjustment to Magic Might.
quotes: you must subtract the character's Size from its Might Score, or add to it if Size is negative

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Character Guides
entries.summary: A shorthand for storyguides: a character guide lists only the required Might, Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Personality Traits, Abilities and Powers for a type of magic character instead of a full sheet.
quotes: The character cannot spend experience points on any other aspect of the character until all of its scores have reached these levels.

entries.title: Magic Human Characters
entries.summary: Magic humans are designed like ordinary human characters but always look monstrous, suffering a social penalty with mundane humans and animals; magi are better designed normally and given a transformation Virtue later.
quotes: giving them a –6 to all social interactions with mundane humans or animals

entries.title: Magic Thing Characters
entries.summary: Magic things draw their Might from Size according to a minimum-Size table, can grow in Might by joining a larger entity, move slowly, are not blocked by Magic Resistance unless using an active supernatural effect, and always have Temporary Might.
quotes: The following chart shows the minimum Size required for each level of Might Score.
Magic things always have Temporary Might
All magic thing characters receive the No Fatigue Quality at no cost.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition p.64 Hermetic Empowerment
The Mysteries Revised Edition p.66 Spirit Familiar
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.134 Bind Magical Creatures

entries.title: Cunning Characters
entries.summary: Notes on the limits of playing an unintelligent character, and the option to convert Cunning to Intelligence when the Magic realm significantly changes it.
quotes: They cannot use Confidence Points unless they have the Ferocity Virtue.

entries.title: Magic Spirit Characters
entries.summary: Magic spirits are designed from a physical form's Characteristics but are insubstantial, can be affected only by beings of the same form, are immortal unless their true form is destroyed, and always have an innate Magical Air.
quotes: Magic spirits always have an innate Magical Air that is very difficult for them to overcome.

entries.title: Magic Character Season
entries.summary: Season replaces age for magic characters and determines starting experience points: spring, summer, autumn or winter stages of development, with Abilities bought according to Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: Season is a new statistic that replaces age for magic characters
| Winter | 1200 |

entries.title: Magic Might (character creation)
entries.summary: Choose a Magic Might Score and Form from a table by saga power level and role (grog, companion, magus); the Might Score also gives an equal number of points for Magic Qualities, and is subtracted from all Advancement Totals.
quotes: You must subtract the character's Might Score from all Advancement Totals
Minor Qualities cost 1 point, and Major Qualities cost 3 points.

entries.title: Magic Character Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Final steps: at least three Personality Traits, Reputations, starting Confidence for eligible characters, an Essential Trait for its true form, combat scores, equipment and inherent vis.
quotes: (this is typically equal to its Might Score divided by 5, rounded up)

entries.title: Magic Powers
entries.summary: How Magic Qualities give powers designed like Hermetic effects, with a table of spell levels, effect types, Might costs and Initiative for each Quality, plus rules for constant powers, Penetration, Incapacitating wounds and a zero Might pool.
quotes: Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost) + Penetration bonus
Like Ritual spells, Ritual Powers are always at least Level 20, and all powers with effects of Level 50 or more must be designed as Ritual Powers.

related.text: ArM5 p.191 Penetration for Magic Powers

entries.title: Qualities and Inferiorities
entries.summary: Magic Qualities and Inferiorities are the Virtue and Flaw equivalents for characters with a Might Score; they are bought with points equal to Might, need not balance, and grogs may not take Major ones.
quotes: A character starts with a set number of Quality points equal to its Might Score

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.104-109 Heroic Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Major Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Qualities a magic character can buy, including Fatigue Mastery, Focus, Greater and Ritual Powers (with their Might costs and Initiative), Gentle Air, Gifted, Gigantic with its Size table, Improved Characteristic, Natural Appearance, No Fatigue and Vis Mastery.
quotes: The power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2)

entries.title: Minor Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Qualities, such as Form Resistance, Gift of Speech, the Improved Abilities, Attack, Damage, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Powers, Recovery and Soak options, Lesser Power, Minor Virtue and Personal Power.
quotes: Personal Powers have a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Improved Abilities: You gain 50 experience points, which may be spent on any Abilities or Arts that the character can learn.

entries.title: Major Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Inferiorities, such as Acclimation Prone, Major Flaw, Miniature with its Size table, Monstrous Appearance, Reduced Characteristic and Temporary Might, which ties wounds to Might Points and vis.
quotes: When the character is injured, it loses Might Points equal to the penalty of the wound

entries.title: Minor Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Inferiorities, such as Limited Gestures, Movement and Speech, Minor Flaw, the Reduced Abilities, Attack, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Power and Soak options, and Susceptible to Deprivation.
quotes: Reduced Abilities: Subtract 50 experience points from the character's existing Abilities

entries.title: (Form) Resistance (Ability)
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability for characters with Magic Might that adds its score to resistance against damage from things of one Form and raises Magic Resistance against spells of that Form, but does not stack with the Parma Magica.
quotes: You may add the character's score in this Ability as a bonus to attempts to resist damage from things of that Form

entries.title: Magical Meditation (Ability)
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability for characters with Magic Might that lets them recover Might Points faster in a Magic aura while concentrating, and prevent Acclimation at an increased rate.
quotes: it recovers 1 Might Point for each level of the Magic aura over the course of about ten minutes

entries.title: Magic Character Advancement
entries.summary: Magic characters can gain and spend experience points like other characters, but their Might Score is subtracted from the Advancement Total; consuming vis reduces that penalty.
quotes: the character's Might Score is always subtracted from its Advancement Total
If the character consumes a pawn of magic vis of any type, he may reduce the penalty to his Advancement Total by two

entries.title: Magic Qualities and Initiation Scripts
entries.summary: Describes how a rare book could teach a magic being new Magic Qualities, treated like an Initiation Script adapted by a Mystagogue.

entries.title: Transformation
entries.summary: Experience points can be spent to gain, swap or upgrade Magic Qualities and Inferiorities according to a cost table, or vis can be consumed as a transformational study source.
quotes: Practicing a Quality that you already possess with the intention of improving upon it has a Study Total of 5
The character must use a number of pawns of vis of any type equal to its Might Score.

entries.title: Acclimation
entries.summary: Each year a magic character that stays away from Magic loses a Magic Quality or a point of Might unless it meets one of three protective conditions.
quotes: a magic character either loses a Magic Quality, or else reduces its Might Score by 1

entries.title: Acclimation: Auras
entries.summary: A table of the minimum Magic aura strength, by Might Score and time spent within it, needed to avoid Acclimation, with a rule for visiting the Magic Realm.
quotes: treat the Magic Realm as an aura of 10 and halve the character's Might Score

entries.title: Acclimation: Effects
entries.summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation by affecting, or being affected by, a non-Might character with magic for a number of seasons each year, given by a table of Might or effect level.
quotes: a magic character with Might 15 would need to constantly affect a mundane character for three seasons every year

entries.title: Acclimation: Vis
entries.summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation for a year by consuming a Might-based number of pawns of vis, and then rolls on the Vis Consumption chart.
quotes: A magic character is safe any year in which it consumes (Magic Might Score / 2) pawns of magic vis, of any type.

entries.title: Vis Consumption
entries.summary: A stress-die chart for the side effects, botches, story events and Transformation that result when a magic character consumes vis to avoid Acclimation.
quotes: roll a stress die and consult the following chart. The number of botch dice is equal to the number of pawns of vis consumed.

entries.title: Magic Kin
entries.summary: Introduces magic kin lineages that can be used as templates for magic characters, each with Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws to take at character creation.
quotes: that characters designed to belong to that family should strongly consider taking during character creation

entries.title: Atlanteans
entries.summary: Template for ocean-dwelling Atlantean characters with water-based Inherited Virtues, an exile Flaw and powers working over water-ways.
quotes: Other water creatures will only obey a summons if a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor of 6 + Creature Size is successfully made.

entries.title: Flame Dancers
entries.summary: Template for people possessed by the power of fire, with fire-related powers and compulsions.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Let the Bonfire Burn, Personal Power: Endurance of the Flame Dancer

entries.title: Forgotten Gods
entries.summary: Template for old gods who survive in living form, built around a Focus or Greater Power describing their sphere of influence.
quotes: As characters, they should take a Greater Power or Focus Power that describes this influence.

entries.title: Loamwalkers
entries.summary: Template for tree-spirits living in human shape, with powers to travel between trees and change between tree and human form.
quotes: Common Flaws: Dark Secret (Loamwalker), Essential Flaw (minor): Antisocial (Presence), Fear (fire), Baneful Circumstances (must be rooted into the earth)

entries.title: Lost Children
entries.summary: Template for abandoned children who became ageless Magical beings, designed with a child's Size and Characteristic penalties.
quotes: so to play one you should design a character with the Size and Characteristics penalties of a child

entries.title: Men of the Lake
entries.requires: Magic kin: Man of the Lake
entries.summary: Template for sentient lake beings with water powers, a seasonal society and a network of lake regiones.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Drown (see page 137), Personal Power: Simulacrum Form, Ritual Power: Command the Waters, Focus Power: Memory of Water, (Lake) Regio Network.

entries.title: Orphan Born
entries.summary: Template for humans conceived beyond the veil of the spirit world, who can become incorporeal and see spirits.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Incorporeal Form, Personal Power: Ghostly/Physical Form, Second Sight

entries.title: People of the Clouds
entries.requires: Magic kin: Person of the Clouds
entries.summary: Template for sky-sailors who command the wind and can fly or sail ships through the air.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Sail the Wind

entries.title: The Stoneskinned
entries.summary: Template for people of living rock whose stone powers scale with age or Might and who turn to stone in daylight.
