quotes: These stats are Init +X, Atk +2X, Dfn +X, Dam +2X, where X is either the character's (Might Score / 5) or his (age / 10).

entries.title: Warders of Mystery
entries.summary: Template for the society of Auditores who keep magic secret, with a power to perceive distant places through Arcane Connections.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Perceive the Distant Truths

entries.title: Spirits as Characters
entries.summary: Spirits are incorporeal, immortal beings that cannot affect or be sensed by matter without powers or magic, communicating through Silent Speech, and take the Magic Spirit Virtue.

entries.title: Spirit Concept
entries.summary: How to set Characteristics for spirits, that Size is meaningless until a spirit takes physical form, and that all spirits have the Magical Air Flaw.
quotes: For plants and spirits of non-living objects, assume that all Characteristics begin at zero and apply 7 characteristic points in the usual fashion.

entries.title: Taxonomy of the Invisible World
entries.summary: Defines the terms spirit, genius, animus, Daimon and Airy Spirit used for the rules in this chapter.

entries.title: Spirit Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Which seasons suit different kinds of spirits and why spirits often take Reduced Abilities.

entries.title: Spirit Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Spirits need no Quality to be incorporeal or immortal, but need Powers to be seen or to affect the world, so most of their Qualities go to Powers.

entries.title: Spirits as a Source of Vis
entries.summary: Explains how much raw vis a spirit contains, when it can be distilled after the spirit is slain, and the vis from corporeal bodies and Presence.
quotes: typically 1 pawn of an appropriate Form per magnitude of their Might

entries.title: Daimons
entries.summary: Daimons, the Named Spirits, remain in the Magic Realm and act on Earth only through short-lived Aspects with their own Might, which are constant Arcane Connections to the parent.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.

entries.title: Pseudoelementals
entries.summary: Introduces pseudoelementals, creatures similar to elementals but not made of pure elemental matter, which lose Might from Wounds and may lose some vis as they are damaged.
quotes: it loses Might points equal to the penalty it suffers from Wounds

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.133 Elementals

entries.title: Animae as Enchanted Devices
entries.summary: Explains how to treat animae in play: they are enchanted devices, so they hold no vis and are immune to Might-stripping but not to Disenchant, their Might acts as Magic Resistance, and their powers follow magic-item rules for uses per day and Penetration. Hostile auras lower their Magic Resistance and Penetration but do not stop them affecting themselves or ordinary people.
quotes: The primary function of their Might Score is to provide them with Magic Resistance.
The powers of animae work like those of Hermetic magic items in terms of uses per day and Penetration.

entries.title: Damage Levels and Repair of Animae
entries.summary: Animae track damage as object-style Damage Levels instead of Wound Penalties. Damage past Soak forces a Stamina roll to avoid losing a level, they do not heal naturally, and craftsmen with the right Ability can repair levels each season.
quotes: Whenever an anima suffers damage exceeding its Soak, it must make a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor equal to the amount by which the damage exceeded the Soak.
Maahes and Ailuros each have 5 Damage Levels.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.128

entries.title: The Magogoli
entries.summary: Shows how to build Magogoli troopers, generals and spirit summoners by adjusting existing character templates with Giant Blood, Magic Human and Gigantic features, and notes how a Nightwalking summoner without a Might score interacts with wards.
quotes: A common trooper is a grog character, although he also has the Giant Blood Virtue on top of his normal allotment.
it has no Magic Might and so cannot be affected by spells targeting a creature's Might

related.text: Realms of Power: the Infernal p.119
The Cradle and the Crescent pp.179-184

entries.title: Dragon-Born (Magic Kin)
entries.summary: Explains dragon-born human offspring of zmajevi as a type of Magic Kin who buy Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws at character generation and can be identified with Second Sight.
quotes: Dragon-born are another type of Magic Kin

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.89 Magic Kin

entries.title: The Sibyls (magic humans bound to their auras)
entries.summary: Overview of the sibyls as ancient immortal magic humans who each dwell in a powerful Magic aura or regio and risk losing their powers through Acclimation if they leave it.
quotes: Each sibyl rests in a powerful Magic aura or regio, and cannot leave without risking losing her prophetic powers

entries.title: The Sibyllides (children of sibyls)
entries.summary: Describes the children of sibyls as magic kin who always have prophecy- or sight-related powers and who must report back to their mother periodically.
quotes: They are obligated to return to their mother's home every decade to report to her what they have learned about the world

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 89 (magic kin)
Realms of Power: Magic, page 95 (Warders of Mystery)

entries.title: Character Guide: A Sibyl (magic character template)
entries.requires: Being type: Magic Human / Magic character
entries.summary: A minimal-statistics template for a sibyl built with the Magic Characters rules, with notes on the five points of Virtues and Flaws, Magic Might, and the Enigmatic Essential Trait that prevents her speaking clearly.
quotes: The sibyl's Enigmatic Personality Trait is an Essential Trait; magical effects to make her speak clearly mysteriously fail.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 7 (Divination & Augury)

entries.title: Blemmyae Characters
entries.summary: Describes the physical traits of Blemmyae and the Magic Qualities and Inferiorities they inherit as Magic Humans, with differences between male and female Blemmyae and notes on armor and shields.
quotes: Male Blemmyae also have the Age Quickly Major Flaw as a Magic Inferiority, meaning that they have a lifespan typical of that of a human.
They cannot use large shields effectively.

entries.title: Daimons and Aspects
entries.summary: Rules for Daimons, named spirits that stay in the Magic Realm and act on Earth through expendable Aspects, each with its own Might and Might pool. Covers how Aspects are created, destroyed, summoned and bound, and how to give a Daimon statistics if the characters ever confront one.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.
An Aspect cannot appear within several miles of another Aspect of the same Daimon
Ordinary Hermetic magic cannot summon an Aspect of a Daimon from the Magic Realm

related.text: Dies Irae, The Twilight of the Gods

versions.title: Daimons and Aspects
versions.summary: Explains how Magic Realm Daimons act in the world through Aspects: spirits with their own Might that serve as Arcane Connections to the Daimon, can be recreated when destroyed, and cannot be removed for good by Perdo Vim through an Aspect.
quotes: Creating an Aspect does not cost the Daimon any Might points, and it can have any number of Aspects active at any one time.
An Aspect has its own Might Score, although its Might pool does not replenish
related: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic p.102 Daimons

entries.title: Revenants, the Walking Dead
entries.summary: Introduces revenants as restless dead whose only form is an animate material corpse driven by a spirit, and notes that their physical statistics also serve for spell-animated corpses, which have no Might.
quotes: Such automatons are not supernatural beings and have no Might score (and hence no Magic Resistance).

entries.title: Fighting the Walking Dead
entries.summary: How magic and weapons affect revenants: body and spirit are attacked separately, Incapacitating wounds count as Heavy, Perdo Corpus spells aimed at the living often fail, and legend-specific methods destroy the animating spirit.
quotes: they cannot be Incapacitated; treat Incapacitating wounds as Heavy wounds instead.
Learning the method for destroying a revenant may require a story, or if the storyguide prefers she can assign it an Ease Factor of 9 on an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll.

entries.title: Option: Resistance to Piercing Weapons
entries.requires: Revenant creatures; troupe adopts the option
entries.summary: An optional rule letting revenants resist piercing weapons such as spears and arrows, either with a Soak bonus or total immunity, at the storyguide's judgment of what counts as piercing.
quotes: The troupe may wish to grant revenants an additional +10 Soak bonus against such weapons, or simply rule them totally ineffective.

entries.title: Ghosts in Ars Magica (sidebar)
entries.summary: Sidebar defining how ghosts work in the game: appearance and invisibility, inability to learn or change, solidity to other ghosts, spellcasting as illusion unless they have powers, returning after being defeated, fetters, and the vis left behind.

entries.title: The Daimonic Aspect (sidebar)
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining Aspects: each is an independent fraction of a Daimon with its own Might pool and no fatigue, which cannot be summoned where another Aspect of the same Daimon is or was within a day, and cannot be permanently changed.

entries.title: Daimons: General Rules, Aspects and Pacts
entries.summary: Explains how Daimons act on Earth through Aspects, how they are Banished rather than killed, and how theurgists conjure them to provide powers and services.
quotes: A Daimon also does not respond in person — it sends an Aspect of its spirit.
binding or destroying an Aspect has no effect on the Daimon itself
Daimons are never killed or incapacitated by physical combat

entries.title: Spirit guardians of the basilica (manifesting)
entries.requires: Visiting the Basilica of Ten Thousand Columns
entries.summary: The underworld spirits bound to the basilica may be treated as chthonic and mistaken for Infernal creatures by holiness-sensing Virtues, and can spend Might to manifest in a physical form that can be wounded but not killed.
quotes: All of the spirits here can spend 1 Magic Might point to manifest in physical form (and return to spiritual form at will).

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.123 Sense Holiness and Unholiness

entries.title: Spirit Votary (Virtue and Character Type)
entries.summary: A Free Supernatural Virtue making the character a Mythic Companion who must take Spiritual Pact plus further supernatural Virtues and the Pagan Flaw.
quotes: A Spirit Votary is required to take the Spiritual Pact Virtue (see below), along with either three Minor Supernatural Virtues or one Major Supernatural Virtue.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.103 Blood of Heroes

entries.title: Designing Revenants
entries.summary: Revenants are usually Spring or Summer Magic Humans with the No Fatigue and Improved Soak Qualities to reflect their resilience.
quotes: They should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4: Magic Characters.

entries.title: Powers of the Spirits
entries.summary: Introduces common spirit powers, which must penetrate Magic Resistance, with Ritual-like powers permanently reducing the spirit's Might.
quotes: Naturally, any power that affects another being must penetrate its Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Control Human
entries.summary: A spirit power to direct a human, who may resist with an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor set by the spirit's Might.
quotes: To break free, the target makes an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor equal to 9 + magnitude of spirit's Might.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Donning the Corporeal Veil
entries.summary: A spirit power to create and animate a physical body that shares the spirit's statistics but is limited in Size.
quotes: The body created with this power has the same physical statistics as the spirit, but can have a maximum Size of +1.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Eidolon
entries.summary: A spirit power creating an illusory form visible and audible to material beings.
quotes: Creates an illusionary form that is visible and audible to material beings.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Manifestation
entries.summary: A spirit power to take control of plants or animals by touch, with the amount controlled set by the Might points spent.
quotes: For an extra 2 Might points, a group of ten standard creatures or plants (or the equivalent mass) can be controlled.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Material Anchor
entries.summary: A ritual-like spirit power forming an Arcane Connection to a person or place, or making an object a connection to the spirit, with cost set by duration.
quotes: If the connection is to last for hours or days, then it costs just 1 point; a connection that lasts for weeks or months costs 2 points; years or decades costs 3 points; and indefinite Arcane Connections cost 4 points.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Presence
entries.summary: A spirit power giving awareness of a domain whose size depends on its Might, doubling Might for Tether Strength and yielding yearly vis.
quotes: The area controlled by the spirit can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis of an appropriate Form

entries.title: Spirit Power: Regio
entries.summary: A ritual-like power for a spirit with Presence to form a Magic regio with one or more layers of rising aura strength.
quotes: each additional layer has an aura 2 points stronger than the previous layer, up to a maximum of 10

entries.title: Spirit Power: Stasis
entries.summary: A ritual-like power making a Magic-aura area timeless, so residents' aging points become Warping points and long-term residents cannot leave the aura.
quotes: However, any aging points are applied to the character as Warping points instead.

entries.title: Florae and Fauni
entries.summary: Airy Spirits attached to individual plants and animals, with typical Magic Might range and powers for designing them.
quotes: Most fauni and florae possess Cunning rather than Intelligence.

entries.title: Spirits of the Elements
entries.summary: Airy Spirits tied to individual non-living natural objects, with Might scaling by the object's size and importance and differing outlooks by elemental Form.
quotes: A spirit of an element can be present in any matter that is still in its natural form

entries.title: Imagines, Spirits of Sensation
entries.summary: Airy Spirits embodying sensory species, with Imaginem Might and powers that replicate effects matching their sensation.
quotes: The weakest of these spirits represents a specific incidence of a species, whereas those of Might 10 or more represent more-general qualities.

entries.title: Eidolons, Spirits of Emotions
entries.summary: Spirits of emotion created by humans in contact with strong magic; their Might derives from Personality Flaws or Traits and they can be summoned through an Arcane Connection to a person feeling the emotion.
quotes: Otherwise, the spirit has a Might equal to (5 x Personality Trait).

entries.title: Spirits of Place, Genii Loci
entries.summary: The most powerful Airy Spirits, bound to a locus (a place) rather than an object, with typical powers and a protective relationship to everything in the locus.
quotes: Further, all genii loci possess the Ways of the (Land) Virtue.

entries.title: Jinn
entries.requires: Being type: Jinn (Magic, Faerie or Infernal)
entries.summary: A variety of genii loci from desert lands that can align to Magic, Faerie or Infernal Realms, share a bargain-binding Malediction, and can temporarily transfer their locus.
quotes: it is bound to the agreed terms unless its partner reneges first

entries.title: Lugra, Spirits of Hardship
entries.summary: Parasitic spirits of life's hardships that afflict randomly chosen hosts, with typical Control Human and Mastery powers.

entries.title: The Named Spirits (Daimons and Aspects)
entries.summary: Daimons draw power from True Names and act in the world through Aspects, each of which is built as its own spirit with separate statistics.
quotes: Each Aspect of a Daimon should be created as if it were an independent spirit.

entries.title: Characters Touched by Spirits of Place
entries.summary: Ways characters can gain powers from long exposure to a genius loci: birth Virtues and Flaws, Grant powers, possession, bargains and pacts, communion for Mystery initiation, and Warping.
quotes: Major bargains may constitute a pact (granting the Spiritual Pact Virtue)

entries.title: Ghosts (Apparitions, Shades, Spectres)
entries.summary: Describes the kinds of Magical ghost (apparitions, shades and spectres), how each remembers its life, what ties it to the world and how it can be laid to rest.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, page 36

entries.title: Ghosts as Characters
entries.summary: Ghosts are built as spirits with the Magic Spirit Virtue, and the ability to take material form is treated as a supernatural power that not every ghost has.
quotes: are spirits with no true material form and must have the Magic Spirit special Virtue

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Concept
entries.summary: Steps for building a ghost: choose a Flaw as its worldly tie, generate Characteristics as for a human, give it Magic Spirit and a Magical Social Status, and drop Virtues and Flaws that no longer apply.
quotes: All ghosts should have the special Virtue, Magic Spirit

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which character Season to use for apparitions, shades and spectres according to how much of their living knowledge they retain.
quotes: should usually be designed as Autumn characters.

entries.title: Rules for Ghosts (necropolis)
entries.summary: Simple rules for playing a ghost in the necropolis: Mentem Might, no Fatigue, healing at moonrise, limits on casting spells, and the Leaving the Crypt power.
quotes: has a Mentem Magic Might equal to his highest Ability or Art Score

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic pp.115-118 Ghosts

entries.title: Aspects of a Daimon (the She-Wolf)
entries.requires: Being type: Aspect of a Daimon
entries.summary: Explains how a spirit that creates a material body behaves: it can dismiss and recreate its body, the Daimon can send a new Aspect after a day, Acclimation applies, and spending Might on Virtues and Flaws erodes the Aspect. Also advises how to use such a spirit as a provider of vengeance rather than an antagonist.
quotes: If the Aspect is destroyed, the spirit can send another to the Wolf's Court after a day has passed.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.102 Daimon
Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Acclimation
Realms of Power: Magic p.46 Master of Animal Creatures

entries.title: How the She-Wolf grants revenge
entries.requires: Being type: Aspect of a Daimon
entries.summary: Describes how a spirit judges a petitioner's claim and then bestows Virtues or Flaws through its powers, either permanently (costing Might score as well as pool) or temporarily (Might not recovered while the effect lasts).
quotes: If permanent, the power is a ritual-like power and costs points from the creature's Might score as well as Might pool.
If temporary, the power lasts until the She-Wolf dismisses it, but the Might points spent on this power are not recovered while it is ongoing.

entries.title: Ritual of passing on the power
entries.summary: The optional ritual by which the She-Wolf endows a petitioner, which also gives the spirit an Arcane Connection and sympathetic connections to the recipient.
quotes: This ritual is not strictly necessary, but it provides an appropriate amount of mystery and formality to the seeking of vengeance.

entries.title: Converting a Dead Character to a Spectre
entries.summary: Defines a spectre as a ghost bound to its vocation and gives simple rules for turning a dead character into one: assign a Might by importance, keep Virtues, Flaws and Characteristics where they still apply, and keep only the Abilities of the vocation.
quotes: Might is assigned depending on importance and power, typically between 1 and 20.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic ch.5, pp.115-116

entries.title: Death Which Does Not Die (Muspelli Walking Dead)
entries.summary: How the Muspelli use animated corpses as tireless sentries and levies, noting that their usual Might means an Aegis of the Hearth keeps them out although the Parma gives no protection against their physical attacks, and that Walking Dead without Might exist only as part of an ongoing utiseta.
quotes: Commonly, they possess a Might of 9, and so most covenants' Aegis of the Hearth keeps them outside.

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic p.98 Walking Dead

entries.title: Playing Loki
entries.summary: Advice for a storyguide running a being far cleverer than the storyguide: invent obstacles retroactively to fill loopholes in his plans, but let a genuinely clever player plan succeed.
quotes: the storyguide is justified in inventing new obstacles for the players on the spur of the moment and playing them as if they had always been there

entries.title: Aspects of Loki
entries.summary: Limits on how Loki, a Daimon of kosmokrator rank, creates and uses Aspects: how many copies may exist, the loss of constant communication, regaining Might from vis, and the proximity restriction between Aspects.
quotes: Loki can only have a number of copies of the same Aspect active at any one time equal to the Intelligence Characteristic of that Aspect (with a minimum of one)
an Aspect of Loki cannot come within one mile of a place that another Aspect of Loki has been within the last 24 hours
5 points per pawn if the Form matches their Might, 2 points per pawn otherwise

entries.title: Gifts of the Gods
entries.summary: How an Aspect of Loki can loan one of its powers to another being as a mystical item: the Might cost, the item acting as an Arcane Connection, and what happens if the Aspect is destroyed or the original owner recovers the item.
quotes: The item is an Arcane Connection to the Aspect that created it (not to Loki himself), with a +3 Penetration modifier.

entries.title: Ghosts Animating Statues
entries.summary: Egyptian ghosts prefer to be incarnate and animate statues that resemble their bodies, which is why servant statues (ushabtis) and defacing statues matter to tomb robbers.
quotes: Defacement prevents a ghost animating a statue from ambushing the thieves, and deanimates those already possessed

entries.title: Ghosts Carving Equipment
entries.summary: A ghost buried with carving tools can make representations of objects that become real for its purposes, with creation time depending on the age of the tomb, and can feed itself or summon faerie reinforcements.
quotes: so the ghost can create a new object by drawing it in a single round

entries.title: Possess Statue (Minor Power)
entries.requires: Egyptian ghost with the Possess Statue power
entries.summary: A power letting a ghost animate a wooden, stone or metal statue, given with a Hermetic equivalent level for each material; the statue's physical attacks must penetrate opponents' Magic Resistance.
quotes: Note that the physical attacks of an animated statue have to Penetrate the Magic Resistance of any opponents struck.

entries.title: Quick Ghost Conversion (ka)
entries.summary: A step-by-step kit for turning an ordinary character into an Egyptian ghost (ka): choose Magic Might, swap Virtues and Flaws, add Magic Spirit, note intangibility and vulnerability to Mentem, and add powers and vis.
quotes: Give the character a Magic Might score of between 5 and 25
Add vis, usually Mentem, equal to the Might score divided by 5.

entries.title: Quick Animated Statue Conversion
entries.summary: A kit for building an animated statue from a mortal character, including Soak by statue material, size adjustments to Strength and Quickness, damage penalties for stone or bronze weapons, and how to force a ghost out of a statue.
quotes: Wood grants +9 Soak.
Hard metal grants +21 Soak.
Characters lose 2 Strength and gain 1 Quickness per Size lost, or conversely gain 2 Strength and lose 1 Quickness per Size gained.

entries.title: Royal Pharaonic Ghosts
entries.summary: Guidelines for designing the ghosts of Egyptian royalty: bloodline Virtues from Faerie gods, odd powers drawn from a pharaoh's life, and Transformation after death thanks to long death rituals.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Transformation

entries.title: The Akh (Egyptian Daimon)
entries.summary: Explains how the ba, ka and khu fuse into an akh, a Daimon, and how to build one as a Magic Spirit with a Magic Might range, as a Winter creature summoned by name or relics.
quotes: Assume a Magic Might Score of 20 for noblemen who have the simplest coffin texts, up to 60 for the greatest pharaohs

entries.title: Infernal Creatures: Demon Basics
entries.summary: Introduces demons and devils as one group, notes that some corrupted physical beings with Infernal Might are not true demons, and states that demons can shed their physical forms at will and are not bothered by The Gift.
quotes: All demons can put off their physical forms and revert to being pure spirits at will.
Demons are never noticeably bothered by The Gift.

entries.title: Demonic Powers (Coagulation, Obsession, Envisioning, Possession)
entries.summary: The powers common to demons: Coagulation to form a body, Obsession to impose a sinful Personality Trait on a mortal (with a worked example), Envisioning for dreams and waking visions, and Possession, which uses a separate Possession Might Pool.
quotes: Manifesting a physical form takes a round for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon
the victim's player must make a simple roll and add the Obsession Trait; this must be lower than a simple roll + any other suitable Personality Trait to successfully resist the impulses
the demon may expend any number of points from its Might Pool to create a Possession Might Pool

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.75

entries.title: Demonic Weaknesses
entries.summary: Every demon is vulnerable to expressions of God's power and has one extra weakness chosen from a list (abhorrent material, compulsiveness, ordering, protected group, running water, vulnerability). Learning a particular demon's weakness takes a roll.
quotes: must make an Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9 + (Might /5)
Subtract 3 from the Ease Factor if the demon is a member of a family

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.41

entries.title: Demons and Free Will
entries.summary: Explains that demons always follow their evil impulses and have no virtues, and that Confidence represents a demon's ability to act rationally against its passions; not all demons have it.
quotes: Demons have no virtues at all, which includes such virtues as patience, courage, and self-control.
Not all demons have Confidence, so some demons are incapable of acting against the dictates of their passions.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, Chapter 4

entries.title: Religious Limitations on Demons
entries.summary: Religious restrictions on demons: they lose their physical form and cannot spend Might on Holy Saturday, are driven from Jewish households whose sins are atoned between Yom Kippur and Sukkot, and cannot use Infernal Might directly on a Muslim who has recently completed the hajj.
quotes: In Christian lands, all demons are forced to abandon their physical form at dawn on Holy Saturday

entries.title: Demons, Auras and Regiones
entries.summary: How quickly Infernal creatures regain Might: at a constant daily rate normally, faster in an Infernal aura, and not at all in a Divine aura.
quotes: NUMBER OF HOURS TO RESTORE ALL MIGHT: 24 - (2 x Infernal Aura)
MIGHT POINTS RESTORED PER HOUR: Infernal Might / Number of hours
A demon cannot regenerate any Might in a Divine aura.

versions.title: Demons, Auras, and Regiones
versions.summary: Governs how fast a demon regains Might Points normally, faster in Infernal auras, and not at all in a Divine aura.
quotes: Number of hours to restore all Might in Infernal aura: 24 – (2 x Infernal Aura)
A demon cannot regenerate any Might at all in a Divine aura.

entries.title: What are Demons?
entries.summary: Defines what counts as a demon (any creature with an Infernal Might) and the celestial, terrestrial and Infernal-angel origins, which have no functional differences in play.
quotes: There are no functional differences between any of these groups.

entries.title: The Spiritual Form of a Demon
entries.summary: Rules for a demon in spirit form: unseen and unable to affect matter, immune to non-supernatural wounds and ageing, fast flying, and slain only by loss of Infernal Might.
quotes: spiritual demons may travel ten times faster than a human
can only be slain be effects that deplete its Infernal Might

entries.title: The Physical Form of a Demon
entries.summary: Rules for a demon in coagulated physical form: it can interact with matter and be hurt or slain, heals and ages only in this form, and leaves a corpse that may hold vis.
quotes: typically a pawn for every magnitude of Infernal Might

entries.title: Updating the Bestiary
entries.summary: Guidance for converting the demons in the core rulebook bestiary to the new rules by assigning each an order, the order's general traits and the Powers all demons share.

entries.title: Demonic Might Tables (Order and Rank)
entries.summary: Tables giving the Infernal Might range and relative frequency of ranks for each of the nine demonic orders, plus the extra Infernal Might and equivalent Reputation each rank grants.
quotes: | Master | +5 | 3 |
| Prince | +20 | 9 |

entries.title: Common Demonic Traits
entries.summary: Traits all demons share: Infernal Might, a defining sin as a Personality Trait, and an inability to display virtuous Personality Traits of their own free will.
quotes: A demon automatically fails personality rolls (ArM5, page 18) if succeeding would make it act in a virtuous manner.

entries.title: Demonic Might: Order and Rank
entries.summary: Explains that a demon's Infernal Might comes from its order plus a bonus for its rank, and that the two sources are indistinguishable in play.

entries.title: Demonic Reputations
entries.summary: Demons may have Infernal Reputations known to other demons and infernalists; the highest of these and the rank's equivalent Reputation gives the demon's Hierarchy score used when it is summoned.
quotes: The Hierarchy score of a demon is the highest of any Infernal Reputations it has

entries.title: Demonic Characteristics
entries.summary: How to assign Characteristics to a demon: physical Characteristics are bought with points based on Infernal Might, mental ones with a small allotment, with a minimum physical score and no maximum. Includes example Infernal Reputations.
quotes: Demon Physical Characteristics points: Infernal Might
Demon Mental Characteristics points: 0 – 7 (possibly more for powerful demons)

entries.title: Example Infernal Reputations
entries.summary: Table of example Infernal Reputation titles for each band of Reputation score, useful when giving a demon a Reputation.

entries.title: The Infernal Hierarchy
entries.summary: Introduces the nine-order hierarchy of demons used to classify them, with the caveat that storyguides need not be constrained by it.

entries.title: Infernal Ghosts
entries.summary: How to build an Infernal ghost as a demon: its role determines its order, and it lacks the Coagulation Power and physical statistics.
quotes: Infernal ghosts should be designed like any other demon, except that they have no Power of Coagulation

entries.title: False Gods (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for False Gods: Might limit, usual ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Shroud the Stench of the Pit, The Wealth of Nations and His Master's Voice.
quotes: Personality Traits: Proud +6
for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon

entries.title: Spirits of Deceit (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Spirits of Deceit: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Change Form, Trust of the Innocent, Forked Tongue of the Serpent and The Serpent's Oracle.
quotes: The Size of the altered form is limited to whatever is natural for the species
An Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is allowed to resist the effect.

entries.title: Vessels of Iniquity (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Vessels of Iniquity: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Form of Wickedness (a special Coagulation), Form of Man and Contagious Obsession.
quotes: A Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is needed every hour
For every victim who comes under the sway of the Obsession, the demon loses a point from its Might Pool

entries.title: Avengers of Evil (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Avengers of Evil: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Punish the Sinner Power, whose wound depends on the victim's unatoned sin.
quotes: he suffers a Heavy wound if this Power penetrates his Magic Resistance
a number of points of damage equal to a simple die plus the sum total of all his sinful Personality Traits

entries.title: Demons of God or Infernal Angels?
entries.summary: Clarifies that Avengers of Evil and Accusers claiming to be angels are treated in game terms as demons with Infernal Might.
quotes: both Avengers of Evil and Accusers are demons, because they have Infernal Might rather than Divine Might

entries.title: Deluders (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Deluders: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Delusion and Duplicate the Magi's Technique-based spell effects.
quotes: A minor illusion which affects an Individual amount of material (such as the demon itself) costs one point
It cannot create any effect with a level greater than its Infernal Might, or duplicate Ritual effects.

entries.title: Aerial Powers (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Aerial Powers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Elemental Control and Recalcitrance, which inflates the demon's effective Might against control attempts.
quotes: at a cost of 1 Might Point per magnitude of effect
treats the demon's Might as if it were one-and-a-half times its actual Might

entries.title: Furies (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Furies: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Waxing Tide of Humors, Beserker Rage and Endurance of the Enraged.
quotes: must make a stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9
The Furies do not suffer from wound penalties, except on Defense totals.

entries.title: Accusers (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Accusers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Betrayal of the Heart and Whispers Behind the Back.
quotes: This Power lasts for a month.

entries.title: Tempters & Evil Spirits (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Tempters and Evil Spirits, the largest order: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and Flaws, with no Powers specific to the order.
quotes: Personality Traits: Selfish +5

entries.title: A Life Lacking in Virtue (Demon Psychology)
entries.summary: Demons lack all virtue and cannot be played like immoral humans; spending a Confidence Point lets a demon simulate a virtue for the duration of a situation.
quotes: the expenditure of a Confidence Point allows a demon to simulate a virtue in a particular instance

entries.title: Checklist for Roleplaying Demons
entries.summary: Lists behaviours demons cannot perform and those they can manage only by spending a Confidence Point, derived from their lack of the seven virtues.
quotes: Most demons cannot do the following, except with extreme effort (and spending a Confidence Point, which not all demons have):

entries.title: Demonic Blood
entries.summary: Extended rules for a character with a demon parent: Infernal Might, up to 30 levels of Infernal Powers paid with Might Points, an attendant ruach, accelerated aging, and restrictions on other Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: she is an Infernal being and possesses an Infernal Might (Corpus) score of 5
The Might cost for each Power is equal to its magnitude divided by two (but always at least one point).
increases two years for every year that passes

entries.title: Tainted Characters
entries.summary: Introduces tainted people, children whose creation demons meddle with so that they become tools in the demons' schemes.

entries.title: Characters with Demonic Blood (guidance)
entries.summary: Guidance on demon-blooded characters: sterile, no need to eat but still hungry, short tragic lives, usable as storyguide characters, and unable to have The Gift.
quotes: A demon-blooded character cannot have The Gift because he is a member of the Infernal realm

entries.title: Venatores (demon-hunters)
entries.summary: Describes the Venatores, magi who hunt demons and pass on their lore as an advanced apprenticeship, and how demon-slaying earns them a Venator Reputation and a high Hierarchy Score.
quotes: Each demon they defeat increases their poor Reputation among demons, so that Venatores usually have a powerful Hierarchy Score.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, House Quaesitor, Deals with Devils

entries.title: A Note on The Powers of Demons
entries.summary: Describes three common demonic powers: Coagulation (building a solid body), Envisioning (invading dreams) and Obsession (imposing a temporary Personality trait that may become permanent).
quotes: Manifesting takes (Might) rounds, but dissolving again requires only one round of concentration.
This gives the person a temporary Personality trait equal to the number of points spent

entries.title: Demon Weaknesses
entries.summary: Each demon has a Weakness that characters can learn with a lore roll; a weakness that is a material forces the demon to flee and stops it regaining Might, while a protected group cannot be harmed by it.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against an Ease factor of 9 + (Might / 5)

entries.title: Vampires as Faeries (vitality from blood and fear)
entries.summary: Establishes that Transylvanian vampires are faeries that feed on blood and on the fear their presence causes, gaining vitality whenever peasant rituals repulse them. Every vampire is unique, with its own rites, limitations and vulnerabilities.
quotes: a vampire is a form of faerie that derives vitality both from blood and from the fear its presence engenders
Every time that a vampire is repulsed by the superstitious rituals of a peasant, the vampire's story is enforced, and it gains vitality.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.12 vitality

entries.title: Becoming a Vampire
entries.summary: Lists the folk beliefs about who becomes a vampire and explains that these circumstances merely attract a faerie which takes the vampire role unless the correct propitiatory rites are performed. Correct precautions feed the faerie vitality so that it moves on.
quotes: these rituals in truth feed the faerie vitality, causing it to become sated and to move on

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.12 vitality

entries.title: Precautions Against Vampires
entries.summary: Gives a list of folk precautions of which the storyguide chooses some for each vampire; performing all of them prevents that vampire forming.
quotes: choose one to three items from the following list
If more than one is chosen, all precautions must be met.

entries.title: The Vampire Life Cycle
entries.summary: Describes the phases a vampire passes through from invisible zduhacz to shapeless gadja to human-shaped platenik and finally the long-lived kukudhi, which masquerades as a human and fathers dhampirs.
quotes: Immediately after death, a vampire takes an invisible, ghostlike form (the zduhacz) and haunts the family of the deceased.

entries.title: Creating a Vampire Character
entries.summary: States that vampires are storyguide characters, with only a narrow exception for self-aware kukudhi vampires as possible player characters in a high-power saga.
quotes: Vampires are intended as storyguide characters.

entries.title: Vampiric Virtues, Flaws, and Powers
entries.summary: Lists the Virtues and Flaws every vampire must have when built as a faerie character: a physical form, a cognizance level, a social-interaction trait, Feast of the Dead, a Traditional Ward of sunlight, and the Sap the Life Lesser Power.
quotes: All vampires have the Feast of the Dead Virtue that allows them to obtain vitality from human life, and have a Traditional Ward of sunlight which causes them to take damage if exposed to the light of day.
Finally, all vampires have the Sap the Life Lesser Power (see insert).

entries.title: Common Vampire Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Short lists of Virtues and Flaws commonly given to vampires when designing them as faerie characters.

entries.title: Powers for Vampires (sidebar)
entries.summary: Sidebar of ready-made faerie powers for vampires, grouped as Lesser Powers, Focus Powers and Personal Powers, each with Might cost, Initiative and Hermetic-style parameters.

entries.title: Lesser Powers and Converting to Greater Powers
entries.summary: Explains that each Lesser Power Virtue buys a set number of power levels and gives the conversion to a Greater Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative penalty.
quotes: Each Lesser Power Virtue is a Minor Virtue that grants 25 levels of powers.
halve the Might cost and the penalty to Initiative

entries.title: Sap the Life (vampiric disease power)
entries.summary: A touch power that drains a target's vitality, treated as a disease causing a Light Wound and loss of Fatigue levels, with weekly Disease Recovery Rolls against fixed ease factors. Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.
quotes: he must beat an Ease Factor of 12 to remain stable, and a 18 to improve
the victim loses two Fatigue levels which cannot be regained until the disease has abated

entries.title: Ghost Touch (Focus Power for moving objects)
entries.summary: A variable-cost power letting a spirit move or hurl loose objects, with weight limits that scale with Might spent, extra damage for thrown items, and the option to fight with objects; physical attacks must penetrate Magic Resistance.
quotes: For 1 Might point, a maximum of 5 lbs. can be moved; every additional Might point doubles this weight limit.
the item inflicts +5 damage per Might point spent

entries.title: Vampire Personal Powers (Flight, Invisibility, Silent Motion, Supernatural Agility)
entries.summary: Personal Powers are Minor Virtues buying a fixed number of effect levels; the sidebar gives Flight, Invisibility, Silent Motion and Supernatural Agility with their limits (for example no combat while flying swiftly and no flight when heavily encumbered).
quotes: Personal Powers are Minor Virtues, and each allows a character to buy 25 levels of effects.

entries.title: Vampire Limitations (Traditional Wards)
entries.summary: Describes how folk rituals repel vampires because they feed the faerie vitality, and gives a list of limitations of which one to three are chosen for each vampire.
quotes: For each vampire, pick one to three of the following limitations; the vampire has to obey these rules:

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie Traditional Ward

entries.title: Ways to Kill a Vampire
entries.summary: Explains that the correct folk rituals sate a vampire for good, after which the faerie reforms elsewhere, whereas a botched killing lets it return within days or weeks. Lists methods of dispatch of which one is picked for each vampire.
quotes: For each vampire, pick a method of dispatch that results in permanent death:

entries.title: Magi as Vampire Slayers (sidebar)
entries.summary: Warns that simply destroying a vampire and taking its vis does not end the threat, because the community's psychic wound attracts a replacement vampire until the proper rites are performed.
quotes: Even if a magus extracts the vis from the corpse (killing it permanently), another vampire is attracted by the community's wound and takes up where the other left off.

entries.title: Infernal Vampires (broukolak)
entries.summary: Explains that not all vampires are faeries: a demon can consume a corpse and take the deceased's form, and cursing oneself at death attracts one. Introduces the broukolak and its effect on the surrounding area.
quotes: Sometimes, a demon consumes a corpse, and takes the form of the deceased.

entries.title: Living Vampires
entries.summary: Introduces living vampires, human witches and sorcerers who prey on locals but are not faeries and need not drink blood. When they die they attract powerful vampiric faeries.
quotes: Living vampires are witches or sorcerers, who prey on the locals much like the dead vampires.

entries.title: The Strigoi and Vjestitza (living vampire witches)
entries.summary: Describes the strigoi viu or vjestitza, a witch whose spirit leaves her body at night to feed on the heart-blood of victims and who belongs to a coven. Suggests building them as Nightwalkers, infernal witches or faerie wizards.
quotes: These characters are Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, Chapter 6), but they may have other powers.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie Ars Fabulosa

entries.title: Preventing Vampires (hunter practice)
entries.summary: Explains that vampire precautions are done either to the corpse (feet, hands, mouth) or to the place of death, that they work only against some vampire types, and that the Church objects to routine mutilation.
quotes: Most remedies only work on some vampires rather than being universal solutions

entries.title: Killing Vampires (hunter procedure)
entries.summary: Step-by-step approach to hunting a vampire: identify its type, find its daytime resting place (Scry helps), confirm it, ban the grave to weaken it, then destroy it in the exact required way. Includes tactics such as hunting on a Saturday.
quotes: Hunting a vampire on a Saturday is a common tactic, taking advantage of the frequent limitation on vampires that prevents them from spending Might points on a Saturday.
neither a white stallion nor a gander will step over a vampire's grave

related.text: Chapter 8 Ways to Kill a Vampire

entries.title: Elementals: Rarefication
entries.summary: Describes what elementals are (pure elemental matter given pseudo-life by magic, not truly alive) and how rarefication forms one, including accidental and spontaneous formation in Magic auras. Once formed an elemental does not age, eat or fall ill.
quotes: The process of forming an elemental is called rarefication.
raw elemental matter possessing a Warping Score of 5 may spontaneously rarefy into an elemental

entries.title: Elementals and Might
entries.summary: How elementals regain spent Might: slowly while resting in a suitable Magic aura, or immediately by consuming vis.
quotes: An elemental does not replenish its Might Pool every day, but instead only recovers Might Points when resting in a Magic aura of no less than (its Might Score / 5)
5 Might Points for every pawn of vis associated with the same Form as its Might, or 2 Might Points for every pawn of vis associated with any other Art.

entries.title: Size, Might and Characteristics of Elementals
entries.summary: A table giving an elemental's Size and its eight Characteristics for each Might score from 1 to 50, used when designing a new elemental.
quotes: The Size of an elemental is dependent on the Might chosen for it, and the Might of an elemental also determines its typical Characteristics.

alsoIn.title: Size, Might, and Characteristics of Elementals

entries.title: Magic and Elementals
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic creates, controls, wards and destroys elementals, and how botched spells or lab activity involving an elemental Form in a Magic aura can accidentally rarefy one.
quotes: Ritual Creo spells can create elementals, and they may be controlled using Rego magic.
The production of an elemental is a potential consequence of any botched spell or lab activity involving an elemental Form while in a Magic aura.

entries.title: Elemental Combat
entries.summary: Elementals cannot be wounded in the usual way: each blow also drains their Might Pool, they go inanimate at zero Might, and pieces knocked off in combat carry vis that can be collected or reabsorbed.
quotes: each wound also reduces the elemental's Might Pool by a number of points equal to the Wound Penalty
An Incapacitating Wound removes 5 Might points, just like a Heavy Wound.
a number of pawns equal to ((total Wound penalty /5) – the number of pawns already lost)

entries.title: Elemental Powers
entries.summary: Every elemental has a power from its elemental matter and a power describing its natural attack, plus usually one more. Its natural attack costs no Might points, so its Penetration is typically its Might.
quotes: the elemental does not need to spend Might points for this attack, meaning that its Penetration for this is typically equal to its Might.

entries.title: Earth Elementals (Genomi)
entries.summary: What earth elementals can be rarefied from, how the quantity of raw material limits their Might, how they behave and attack, and which weapons can hurt them.
quotes: Only bludgeoning weapons such as hammers, maces, or axes can damage an earth elemental
They may be rarefied from any large concretion of earth that has not been worked by human hands

entries.title: Earth Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Crush power every earth elemental has (pinning and breaking equipment) and optional powers such as The Red Touch and Slake Thirst, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All earth elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Water Elementals (Lymphae)
entries.summary: What water elementals can be rarefied from, their temperament, movement and attacks, and how weapons and fire affect them.
quotes: A water elemental's attacks only inflict Scuffle damage
Only naturally occurring liquids can produce elementals, typically of salt or fresh water.

entries.title: Water Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Drown power every water elemental has and optional powers such as Chill Touch and Sight of the River, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All water elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Air Elementals (Zephyri)
entries.summary: What air elementals can be rarefied from, their restless nature, perception and movement, and their immunity to weapons.
quotes: Any air under the open sky or any natural weather phenomenon can produce a zephyrus.

entries.title: Air Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Sufficiale suffocation power every air elemental has, including the contested Quickness + Athletics roll to escape, plus optional powers such as Dissolution and Jupiter's Touch.
quotes: All air elementals have the following power:
Compare Quickness + Athletics stress rolls of the victim and the elemental (using Might/5 for the elemental's Athletics), the highest wins.

entries.title: Fire Elementals (Phlegethi)
entries.summary: What fire elementals can be rarefied from, how they feed, move across flammable surfaces and jump gaps, and how weapons and water affect them.
quotes: It may also jump a gap of nonflammable surface (such as bare rock) up to a width equal to its Magic Might in feet.
Larger sources of water quench the elemental's body, inflicting "wounds" as if it were fire damage

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.67

entries.title: Fire Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Burn power every fire elemental has (damage from a stress die plus its current Might pool) and optional powers such as Fascination and Heat of the Searing Forge.
quotes: All fire elementals have the following power:
takes damage equal to a stress die plus the entity's current Might pool

entries.title: New Elementals Spells and Spell Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for creating, converting, controlling and destroying elementals using the elemental Forms.
quotes: Create an elemental from a base amount of elemental matter (Ritual)
Completely control an elemental

entries.title: Designing Elementals
entries.summary: Introduction to building an elemental character as a Magic Thing, with its inherited Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: the general principles can be applied to use an elemental as the starting point for a magic character

entries.title: Elemental Concept and Characteristics
entries.summary: How an elemental's Size and element determine its Characteristics, which Characteristics cannot be negative for each element, and the Size adjustment applied to Quickness and Strength.
quotes: make the usual adjustment from Size, subtracting Size from Quickness and adding twice Size to Strength.

entries.title: Elemental Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Elementals are normally Spring characters and must buy Brawl and Athletics (or Swim for water) to a score tied to their Might, using Improved Abilities if experience runs short.
quotes: Elementals are almost always Spring characters

entries.title: Elemental Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Elemental Might is set by the amount of matter it formed from and fixes its Size, with fixed free Qualities and an obligatory Greater Power for its element.
quotes: Every increase in magnitude of Might (as if it were a spell) adds three to the Size.

entries.title: The Magical Lineages of Cats
entries.summary: Introduces the three cat lineages descended from familiars of the Founders, whose magical features breed almost true.

entries.title: Cat Character Template
entries.summary: A worked template showing how to build a magical cat character from the mundane stats and magical additions.
quotes: Cats may only have 10 points of Qualities
Might divided by 5, rounded up

entries.title: Cats as Example
entries.summary: Explains that the cat section is a model for building power lists for other species, borrowing powers and following the same guidelines.

entries.title: Black Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Black Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: White Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the White Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Tortoiseshell Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Tortoiseshell Lineage, its rare males, and its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Cat Magical Powers
entries.summary: Each purchase of a Greater or Lesser Magical Power Quality gives a cat one power chosen from the lists.
quotes: Players designing cats select one magical power for each purchase of the Greater Magical Power or Lesser Magical Power Qualities.

entries.title: Cats' Greater and Lesser Powers
entries.summary: Rules for the spell-level cost, Penetration Score, Might cost and Initiative Bonus of cat powers.
quotes: A Penetration Score = Might of the cat (5 x the cost of the power) + the cat's Penetration Bonus.
The Initiative Bonus for a Lesser Power is equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude x 2).

entries.title: Warder's Walk
entries.summary: A cat power letting several cats combine their other powers in a ritual to penetrate Magic Resistance, at the risk of a fatal botch as more cats join.
quotes: It is a variant of Wizard's Communion.

entries.title: Black Cat Wards
entries.summary: Describes the ward powers Black Lineage cats use, singly or in procession, to protect a home or settlement against minor faeries and demons.

entries.title: Personal Magical Powers for Cats
entries.summary: Rules for the Initiative bonus, spell-level cost and Penetration Score of personal powers for cats.
quotes: An Initiative bonus equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude /2).

entries.title: Animal Grogs
entries.summary: Introduces animals as grog characters, with guidance on which Sizes and kinds of animal make the best player characters.
quotes: creatures between the Sizes of –3 and +2

entries.title: Animal Physical Form
entries.summary: Explains what an animal body prevents (grasping and using tools) and grants (natural protection, natural weapons and abilities like flight or swimming), and that listed Quality modifiers are not applied.
quotes: which grant an intrinsic Protection of at least 1

entries.title: Animal Cunning Instead of Intelligence
entries.summary: Animals have Cunning rather than Intelligence, act by instinct and Personality Traits, cannot reason logically, and must take the Restricted Learning Flaw.
quotes: The Cunning characteristic possessed by beasts means that they act largely through estimation (also called instinct), and are ruled by their Personality Traits.

entries.title: Animal Language Abilities
entries.summary: Animals cannot speak, have no automatic Native Language, learn human languages slowly depending on Cunning, and have a species Language Ability that cannot be raised with experience.
quotes: an animal always has a Source Quality of (4 + Cunning)

entries.title: Animal Aging Table
entries.summary: A table giving lifespan, starting age, the age aging begins, the modifier to aging rolls and the number of aging rolls per year for humans and several kinds of animal.
quotes: | Hoofed Beasts | 27 | 3 | 20 | +1 per 5 years | 2 per year |

entries.title: Animal Aging Rate
entries.summary: Shows how to scale the human aging figures to any creature's average lifespan, covering the age aging begins, the aging-roll modifier and the number of aging rolls per year, spread across the seasons.
quotes: Thus, a creature with an average lifespan of 10 years has a modifier of (50/10), or 5.

entries.title: Animal Grog Characteristics and Size
entries.summary: Gives how Size, the Large Virtue and Small Frame Flaw affect an animal grog, the penalties to Presence and Communication when dealing with humans by animal type, and how Size adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: After Characteristic points have been decided, add twice the character's Size to her Strength, and subtract the character's Size from her Quickness.

entries.title: Animal Grog Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Lists the intrinsic Flaws every animal grog has without gaining points, the required Restricted Learning Flaw, suitable Social Status options, and how Animal Ken substitutes for a Language Ability.
quotes: Animal grogs suffer from the effects of the No Hands and Mute Flaws

entries.title: Animal Grog Abilities and Experience
entries.summary: Describes the starting experience animal grogs receive for their pre-adult life, their free animal Language Ability, yearly experience, early aging and typical Abilities.
quotes: An animal grog receives 120 experience points for his pre-adult life

entries.title: Dragons and Dragon-kind
entries.summary: Distinguishes serpents, drakes, worms and true dragons, and advises that the largest dragons exceed what the rules can represent and need innovative plans to defeat.

entries.title: Dragons as Characters
entries.summary: Weak dragons can be built with the magical character rules as grogs, companions or magus-equivalents, while non-player dragons need not be strictly balanced.

entries.title: Dragon Concept
entries.summary: Base Characteristics, Size, required Virtues and suggested Virtues and Flaws when designing a dragon or dragon-kin.
quotes: Dragons and their kin have base Characteristics of 0, and 7 points to spend on improving Characteristics (like human characters).

entries.title: Dragon Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which seasons suit serpents and dragons and on giving combat opponents a good Brawl.

entries.title: Dragon Might Score and Qualities
entries.summary: A table of typical Might ranges for each kind of dragon-kin, plus advice on Qualities for breath, gaze and combat statistics.
quotes: A dragon's combat statistics may be improved through liberal use of the Improved Attack, Improved Defense, Improved Damage, and Improved Soak Qualities.

entries.title: Transylvanian Dragons: Realms, Detection and Might
entries.summary: Explains that local dragons belong to the Infernal or Magic realm, how realm-specific Intellego Vim spells tell them apart, and the Might ranges used for weak, typical, powerful and legendary dragons.
quotes: Intellego Vim spells will indicate which realm a creature is associated with, although each Intellego Vim spell must be realm-specific.
Weak dragons have Infernal or Magic Might Scores between 15 and 30, typical dragons between 30 and 40, and the most powerful dragons have Might scores between 40 and 50.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.74 Dragons

entries.title: Infernal Dragons (aždaje)
entries.summary: Describes aždaje as intelligent Infernal beasts rather than demons, their dominance hierarchy, their ability to pose as Magical dragons if they resist Intellego Vim, and their lairs in corrupted Infernal auras.
quotes: Unlike other Infernal beasts, aždaje are intelligent instead of cunning.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.15 Infernal auras

entries.title: Building a Corrupted Dragon
entries.summary: Explains how to create game statistics for a corrupted dragon, either from Infernal and beast Virtues and Flaws or by adding Infernal Virtues and Flaws to a Magic dragon, which then uses Infernal Might.
quotes: In most cases, a corrupted beast is a tainted version of a mundane beast, and game statistics are created by adding Infernal Virtues and Flaws to the mundane beast's existing statistics.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.77-79
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Statistics of Shapechangers
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Introduces the seven-step procedure for combining a human's and an animal species' statistics into those of a shapechanger's animal form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 1: Characteristics
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: For each Characteristic other than Intelligence/Cunning, take the lower value if both are negative, the higher if both are positive, and otherwise add the two.
quotes: If the human and the animal Characteristic are both negative, use the lower of the two.
If the human and the animal Characteristic are both positive, use the higher of the two.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 2: Cunning Versus Intelligence
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Shapechangers normally keep human Intelligence, though lycanthropes lose it for Cunning; a worked example combines a magus's and a wolf's Characteristics.
quotes: In most cases, the shapechanger retains human Intelligence.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 3: Size
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: The animal form uses the animal's Size; a Size-affecting Virtue or Flaw makes the character a notably large or small member of the species.
quotes: Human Size has no impact on the Size statistic of the shapechanged form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 4: Virtues and Flaws
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Virtues and Flaws of both human and animal forms apply in animal form, but a duplicate applies only once.
quotes: If the animal form already has a Virtue or Flaw possessed by the character, it applies only once.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 5: General Abilities
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: A shapechanged character uses the animal form's General Abilities, keeping only languages, lores, Supernatural Abilities and (if Intelligence is retained) Arcane and Academic Abilities.
quotes: Use the General Abilities of the animal form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 6: Communicating
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: A shapechanger can communicate with animals of the same or similar species, grouped by temperament, aspect, diet and habitat.
quotes: Acquire the ability to communicate with members of the same or similar species as the shapechanged form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 7: Wounds and Experience
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Wounds carry between human and animal forms (lycanthropes heal animal-form wounds on reverting), and experience gained in animal form may go to animal-form Abilities.
quotes: Any wounds taken in the human form are reflected in the animal form, and vice versa.

entries.title: Designing Giants
entries.summary: Humanoid beings larger than human size get their Size from the Gigantic Quality.

entries.title: Giant Concept
entries.summary: Story roles and suggested Virtues and Flaws for giants, which use the Magic Human rules with the Gigantic Quality applied after Characteristics.
quotes: Giants should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4.

entries.title: Giant Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Spring giants suffer child-like Characteristic penalties and language Abilities must be bought with the giant's season experience.

entries.title: Giant Might and Qualities
entries.summary: All giants take the Major Quality Gigantic, repeated for larger Sizes, which drives the Might needed.
quotes: All giants must take the Major Quality, Gigantic; giants larger than Size +2 should take it more than once.

entries.title: Giant Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Giants use clubs, with combat statistics computed normally allowing for the Gigantic Quality's effects.

entries.title: Norse Giants and Trolls
entries.requires: Being type: Norse giant or troll
entries.summary: Options for building Norse giants and trolls, including elemental Form affiliations, typical powers and a size-changing rule.
quotes: When the giant reduces its size, its Strength diminishes by 2 and its Quickness improves by 1 for each point of Size reduction.

entries.title: Non-Human Giants
entries.summary: To build oversized elementals, spirits or animals, use the rules for that creature type and add the Gigantic Quality.
quotes: simply choose Gigantic as one of the creature's Qualities

entries.title: Golems (Introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces the golem as the pinnacle of kabbalistic achievement: unliving clay brought to life by Divine energies and usually made to protect a community.
quotes: While Kabbalah is used by Jewish practitioners in place of the Invocation Holy Method, the pinnacle of kabbalistic achievement is the creation of the golem

entries.title: Creating Golems
entries.requires: Ability: Kabbalah; studied the Sefer Yetzirah
entries.summary: Creating a golem takes several seasons: shape clay, then accumulate points toward its Might with an Awaken Golem Total, with a Might cap, botch dice and a limit of one golem per protected community.
quotes: AWAKEN GOLEM TOTAL: Intelligence + Kabbalah + Wonders + Ceremony Bonus + Dominion Aura
AWAKEN GOLEM EASE FACTOR: 30
MIGHT CAP: Kabbalah x 5

entries.title: Standard Golem Traits
entries.summary: Starting attributes for a human-form golem played as a Companion: free Characteristics, fixed Virtues and Flaws, starting Abilities and Personality Traits, and a True Name that cannot change.
quotes: All golems have the Unaging and Improved Characteristics Virtues.
Golems do have a True Name, which is determined during their creation.

entries.title: Empowering Golems
entries.summary: A kabbalist spends seasons designing Holy Powers for a golem and accumulates points with an Empower Golem Total; using powers costs Divine Might points.
quotes: EMPOWER GOLEM TOTAL: Intelligence + Kabbalah + Wonders + Ceremony Bonus + Dominion Aura
A golem may have a number of magnitudes of powers equal to its Divine Might Score.

entries.title: Altering a Golem's Powers
entries.requires: Kabbalist who awakened or empowered the golem
entries.summary: A kabbalist can change a golem's powers, gaining a bonus to the Empower Golem Total by removing an existing power; a worked example follows.
quotes: By removing an existing power, the kabbalist gains a bonus equal to that power's level to his Empower Golem Total.

entries.title: Golem Madness
entries.summary: After a tragedy of hubris, an order to break a mitzvah, or removal from its community, the storyguide rolls a stress die on a table that permanently shifts the golem's Personality Traits or drives it mad.
quotes: the storyguide should roll a stress die, comparing the result to the table below.

entries.title: Destroying a Golem
entries.summary: Gives the three ways to destroy a golem, and how a trusting golem can be commanded into torpor by a member of its community.
quotes: There are three ways of destroying a golem.

entries.title: Beasts of Virtue
entries.summary: Introduces Beasts of Virtue, rare epitomes of their species that make good familiars, and notes the vis contained in their corpses.
quotes: The corpse of a Beast of Virtue typically contains 1 pawn of vis for each 5 points (or fraction) of Might it possessed

entries.title: Designing Beasts of Virtue
entries.summary: Beasts of Virtue use the Chapter 4 magical character rules with set Inherited Virtues and Flaws and no physical-defect Flaws.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Magic Animal; Essential Virtue (Major or Minor)

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Concept
entries.summary: Rules for Characteristics, the required Magic Animal and Essential Virtues, and permitted Virtues and Flaws when creating a Beast of Virtue.
quotes: You have 7 points to spend on Characteristics, just as other characters.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: How a Beast of Virtue's season of life sets its age and how its experience points must be spent on species Abilities.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Guidance on spending Might on Magical Qualities, with powers restricted to those that express the species' perfection.
quotes: determine its Might and spend these points on Magical Qualities, taking Magical Inferiorities if you want more points to spend

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Natural weapons, Protection and species Qualities for animals, and the reminder to subtract Size from initial Might.
quotes: Remember to subtract the Size of a Beast of Virtue from the initial Might score to get the final Might score.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Corrupted Beasts
entries.summary: The restricted list of Virtues and Flaws a corrupted beast may take.
quotes: Virtues: Greater Immunity, Greater Infernal Power, Ferocity, Lesser Immunity, Lesser Infernal Power

entries.title: Corrupted Beast (Flaw)
entries.summary: The compulsory Flaw that gives an animal an Infernal Might, a sinful Personality Trait, a repellent appearance and the Tainted with Evil Flaw, while leaving it unbothered by The Gift.
quotes: The creature has been corrupted by Infernal power, and has acquired an Infernal Might of 5.
Corrupted Beasts do not react negatively to The Gift.

entries.title: Greater Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts)
entries.requires: Virtue: Greater Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts only)
entries.summary: How to design a corrupted beast's Greater Infernal Power as a spell-like effect, with its Might cost, initiative bonus and level cap.
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the Corrupted Beast's (Infernal Might + 10).
A Greater Power typically costs its magnitude in Might points to activate, and has an Init bonus equal to Qik + magnitude.

versions.title: Greater Infernal Power (corrupted beasts)
versions.summary: Rules for giving a corrupted beast a Power that must penetrate, designed with the Maleficia rules, including level cap, Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: with a level of effect that cannot exceed the corrupted beast's (Infernal Might + 10)
has an Initiative bonus equal to Quickness + magnitude

entries.title: Lesser Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts)
entries.requires: Virtue: Lesser Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts only)
entries.summary: How to design a corrupted beast's Lesser Infernal Power, which is cheap to use and cannot need a Penetration total (otherwise it counts as a Greater Power).
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the Corrupted Beast's Infernal Might.
A Minor power typically costs 0-2 Might points to activate, and has an Init bonus equal to magnitude.

versions.title: Lesser Infernal Power (corrupted beasts)
versions.summary: Rules for giving a corrupted beast a constant or cheap Power that needs no Penetration Total, including level cap, Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the corrupted beast's Infernal Might.
adds 2 to the Infernal Might of the corrupted beast

entries.title: Ferocity (animal Confidence)
entries.summary: Gives an animal a Confidence score that it may only use in situations that trigger its corrupt nature.
quotes: in such circumstances the creature has 3 Confidence Points

entries.title: Creatures of Lunar Fire
entries.summary: Lunar-sphere creatures are built as ordinary Magical or mundane animals with the added Lunar Animal Quality.
quotes: All creatures from the lunar sphere and beyond possess the Lunar Animal Quality, reflecting their strange physiognomy.

related.text: ArM5 Realms of Power: Magic (Magical Animals)
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (mundane animals)

entries.title: Lunar Poisoned Waters
entries.requires: Water contaminated by the lunar sphere
entries.summary: Rules for contaminated and aetheric lunar water, treated as a poison and as vitriol respectively, and how Perdo Aquam or Experimental Philosophy can purify it.
quotes: Treat such water as a poison causing a Light Wound with an Ease Factor of 9 to resist if ingested.
(stress die + 9 in this case)

related.text: ArM5 Art & Academe p.67 Experimental Philosophy

entries.title: New Animal Quality: Lunar
entries.summary: Defines the Lunar Animal Quality: invisible bodies that dissolve into aether, and attacks that sap the victim's highest Personality Trait which the creature can use like Ferocity.
quotes: For each point of wound penalty inflicted, the victim loses one point off their highest Personality Trait.

entries.title: Forests of the Dead (Lunar Plants)
entries.summary: How Lunar plants and their spores grow, hide and attack a host, with the Perception roll to notice a spore and the spore's attack, defense and Stealth bonuses.
quotes: This gives the seed +6 to attack, +9 to defense, and +9 to Stealth rolls.
characters make a Perception + (Awareness or Hunt) roll against the seed's Dexterity + Stealth (+9, as above)

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.33 faint traces

entries.title: The Lunar Infection (disease)
entries.summary: Disease statistics and symptoms for infection by a Lunar spore, which paralyses the body and gradually erodes the victim's most distinctive Personality Trait.
quotes: Severity 18 Stable 6, Improve 18, Interval: Week

related.text: ArM5 Art & Academe pp.45-51 disease rules

entries.title: Transformed Animals
entries.summary: Distinguishes Transformed Animals, which are Warped by magic and gain no Magic Might, from Beasts of Virtue.

entries.title: Warping of Animals
entries.summary: Animals gain Warping points like people and acquire Flaws and then a Virtue at set Warping Scores.
quotes: Once an animal gains a Warping score of 1 it acquires a Minor Flaw, and it gains another Minor Flaw when its Warping score reaches 3.

entries.title: Warped Livestock (Covenant Hook)
entries.summary: A covenant with Warped animals may farm them for Muto vis, represented by a vis source Boon.

entries.title: Intentionally Warping an Animal
entries.summary: A cage of change is an enchanted device that gives a captive animal Warping points to make it monstrous for harvesting Muto vis.
quotes: the cage gives the captive in the cage 5 Warping Points

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws from Warping
entries.summary: Lists the Supernatural Virtues and Flaws a magically Warped animal may gain, culminating in a Lesser Power at Warping Score 5.
quotes: eventually acquiring a Lesser Power when it reaches a Warping Score of 5

entries.title: Awakened Trees
entries.summary: Trees in Magic auras are awake, with wakefulness rising with aura strength, and have Cunning instead of Intelligence and no Might score.
quotes: In an aura of level 6 or higher, the trees are fully awake and can see and hear about as well as a human can.

related.text: ArM5 p.137 Stir the Slumbering Tree

entries.title: Animated Trees
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: How trees become mobile through spells or spirit powers, and when an animated tree has a Might score.
quotes: temporarily gains Might equal to the activation cost of the power

entries.title: Character Guide: An Animated Tree
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: Stock statistics block to use for any animated tree, with guidance on uprooting and moving it via Manifestation.
quotes: Under most circumstances, an animate tree has no Might score.

related.text: ArM5 p.139 Lord of the Trees

entries.title: Option: Brawl Skill for Animated Trees
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: Optional rule giving each animated tree its own Brawl skill, set by the caster's Finesse or by the animating spirit.
quotes: a tree animated by a spell has a Brawl skill equal to the caster's Finesse

entries.title: Overrun (creature Quality)
entries.requires: Creature with the Overrun Quality (hippopotamus, elephant)
entries.summary: A charging creature that hits with Overrun knocks its opponent down on a failed Dexterity + Athletics stress roll, after which the opponent is prone and cannot parry. The rule appears in the hippopotamus stat block and is reused for the elephant.
quotes: the opponent must make a Dexterity + Athletics stress roll against an Ease Factor equal to (Damage Total (before soak) + hippopotamus's Size – opponent's Size)

entries.title: Roll Attack and Drowning (crocodile)
entries.requires: Creature with the Roll Attack Quality (crocodile)
entries.summary: A crocodile that has bitten a foe can roll next round to tear flesh or drag the victim underwater to drown, and a victim breaks free only by overcoming a Grapple. The block also gives stealth, ambush and Crushing Jaws notes.
quotes: doing +6 damage without an attack roll
This requires the character to overcome a successful Grapple attack with a Grapple Strength of 10.

entries.title: Crushing Jaws (creature Quality)
entries.requires: Creature with the Crushing Jaws Quality (hyena, crocodile)
entries.summary: A new animal Quality for creatures with tremendously powerful biting muscles; the jaws can be held shut with a successful Grapple.
quotes: This Quality adds +3 Damage to any bite attack.

entries.title: Constriction and Swallow Whole (giant serpents)
entries.requires: Creature with the Constriction or Swallow Whole Quality
