entries.summary: Rules for a serpent that constricts a grappled victim (deprivation checks) and can swallow smaller prey whole, where stomach acid does damage each round unless the victim braces against immersion. Includes group-attack tactics against elephants.
quotes: The victim must make a Stamina check every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.
The powerful acids inflict +9 damage every round, complete immersion quadruples this to +36

entries.title: Forest Spirit General Powers
entries.summary: Rules for a forest's Might score and the three powers every forest spirit has: Presence, Manifestation (controlling animals or growing plants) and Produce Vis.
quotes: but all forests have a Might of at least 30
For a cost of 5 points of Might, a single Size 0 creature (or an equivalent mass of smaller creatures) can be controlled.
a yearly harvest of vis, of a number of pawns up to the Might score

entries.title: Forest Spirit Specific Powers
entries.summary: A catalogue of optional powers a forest spirit can buy with Might (weather control, granting Virtues and Flaws, victory, guidance, healing, possession, oath-enforcement, regiones, shrouding and stasis), with costs, initiative and Forms, and a note that spirits have only Might, Personality Traits and powers.
quotes: 5 points for Minor Flaw, 10 points for Major Flaw, Init 0, Vim
A supernatural power requires 1 Might point per magnitude to produce, in addition to the Might cost (if any) to the possessed.
10 points per level, Init 0

entries.title: The Passage of the Seasons (Might Pools by Month)
entries.summary: A month-by-month record of the Might Pools and faerie auras of the four seasonal courts as they struggle through the year, for the storyguide to track.
quotes: King Holly (Might Pool 35) slays King Oak (Might Pool 15)

entries.title: The Courts of the Seasons
entries.summary: Describes four linked faerie forests ruled by seasonal lords, with Might, traits and powers, and the rule by which each ruler's Might Pool and aura rise and fall through the year.
quotes: Throughout the year they retain a Might Score of 30, used for Magic Resistance and Penetration
Every month following the height of their power, they lose 5 Might points to their opposing court

entries.title: Drowned Men
entries.summary: Drowned Men are sailors who passed through a magical regio and returned as creatures of Magic.

entries.title: Drowned Men Characters
entries.summary: Drowned Men must take the Transformed (Being) Virtue and commonly have a sea Flaw, Greater Immunity (drowning) and the Servant of the Ocean Flaw.

entries.title: Planning for Drowning
entries.summary: A character can try to become a Drowned Man by contacting and bargaining with a powerful water entity before surrendering to the water, using two rolls.
quotes: Determine Contact Method: Int + Magic Lore + Stress die vs Ease Factor of 12
Negotiation for Power: Int + Bargain + Stress Die vs Ease Factor of 6 + Might / 5

entries.title: Burned and Buried Men
entries.summary: A person might be saved from fire or burial by a magical creature of Ignem or Terram and gain Virtues like a Drowned Man.

entries.title: Adulterations: Lingering Problems
entries.requires: House Criamon (any magus may create them)
entries.summary: Explains adulterations, supernatural beings and places made from a magus's psychic debris, as an added consequence of bad Twilight experiences. Resolving one can yield a Twilight benefit.
quotes: This potential Twilight consequence should be considered an addition to the list of bad Twilight effects on ArM5, page 89.

entries.title: Designing Adulterations
entries.summary: Guidelines for designing adulterations as creatures or places, including their Magic Might range, how they bypass their creator's Aegis, and how adulterous regiones behave.
quotes: Each has a Magical Might score that ranges from 10, for minor adulterations, to 45, for the malignancies.

entries.title: Example: Introducing an Adulteration
entries.summary: Worked example of a storyguide turning a bad Twilight outcome into an adulteration and resolving it, with a small reduction in the related Personality Trait.
quotes: She does lose one point from her Angry Personality Trait

entries.title: Creatures of the Divine: General Rules
entries.summary: General rules for beings with Divine Might: ordinary Magic Resistance and Penetration rules apply, they are not omnipotent, they cannot have True Faith, and they are never bothered by The Gift.
quotes: Creatures with Divine Might use the normal rules for determining Magic Resistance, Penetration, and whether their powers can be dispelled.
Creatures with Divine Might cannot have True Faith.
Creatures with Divine Might are never bothered by The Gift.

entries.title: Nephilim
entries.summary: Describes the Nephilim, half-angelic giants, including their longevity, immunity to disease and need to eat prodigiously.

entries.title: Grigori, the Watchers
entries.summary: Describes the Watchers, a tenth Choir cast to Earth and trapped in their Mantle, and how they can be permanently slain.

entries.title: Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: Describes the cloud regio of Nephelococcygia, how to enter it, and the Inherited Virtues and Flaws of the intelligent birds who live there.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Homing Instinct, Keen Vision, Lightning Reflexes.
an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: The set of Greater Powers available to Birds of Nephelococcygia, each given with its Hermetic guideline breakdown.

entries.title: Bird Flight
entries.summary: Flight is natural to these birds and needs no roll under normal conditions; difficult conditions call for a flying roll.
quotes: he has an initiative of Qik + Athletics (flying) for this maneuver
a roll (Dexterity + Athletics(flying) + stress die) may be required to take to the air

entries.title: Stoicheia (place-guardian faeries)
entries.requires: Being type: Stoicheion (faerie spirit of place)
entries.summary: Overview of the Greek spirits of places and the kinds they take (koukouvaounes, basiliskoi, pergalioi, kalotyches), with the powers and wards typical of each.
quotes: Like portunes, the basiliskoi usually have a Focus Power for Domestic Work.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, page 106 (genii loci)

entries.title: Character Guide: Stoicheion (faerie guardian template)
entries.summary: A faerie character template with its Virtue and Flaw budget and powers, including the Guardian of the Bounds ward power with its Might cost and the Extended Glamour vis yield.
quotes: The power costs 1 Might point per 5 levels (or fraction) of the equivalent spell.
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of Animal vis, which manifests as physical objects within the controlled region.

entries.title: A Magical Trainer
entries.summary: Taming points per season for a character with the Master of (Form) Creatures Virtue, using Might, Animal Handling and Animal Ken minus the creature's Might.
quotes: Trainer's Might + Trainer's Animal Handling + Trainer's Animal Ken – Creature's Might

entries.title: Animal Ken and Animals
entries.summary: A character with Animal Ken can reason with any animal using Animal Handling to get it to follow an instruction without taming it, and can give tamed animals more complex commands.

entries.title: Anima damage levels and repair (glass submarine)
entries.summary: Stat block of an awakened iron simulacrum, with the special rule that it tracks Damage Levels like a commercial product rather than Wound Penalties, and can only be repaired by a character with Mechanica or Automata.
quotes: Roll the anima's Stamina (+1) plus a stress die against an Ease Factor equal to the excess damage.
If a character has one of these Abilities, she can repair a number of Damage Levels equal to her score in a season.

entries.title: Some Unusual Pets
entries.summary: Introduces game statistics for a few mundane pets (magpie, monkey, squirrel) built with the animal Qualities rules from Mystery Cults. Pets may be trained by their owners and the statistics can serve as templates for Magical Animal Companions.
quotes: These animals may be trained by their owners.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.40

entries.title: Contained Spirits
entries.summary: Rules of thumb for creatures trapped in containers: bargains bind only the words spoken, a spirit can be won as a permanent ally by favors comparable to Mystery Ordeals, and freeing a faerie unconditionally invites a gift in return.
quotes: A bargain struck with these beings is binding, but only the specific words, not the intent, need to be adhered to.
A rescued spirit may be converted into a permanent ally by performing a series of favors for it.

entries.title: Oleron: Stone Couches and Sleepers
entries.summary: Rules-flavored explanation of how tumuli grow faerie duplicates of folk heroes over years, how a Sleeper's powers and Might follow the hero's folklore and Reputation, when Sleepers wake, and what happens if an ordinary human is buried in a Couch.
quotes: A tumulus will build a skeleton for its hero after three years, and grow his flesh over the next eighteen.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults (Mystery of Becoming)

entries.title: Jinn (Free Virtue)
entries.requires: Virtue: Jinn (spirits of the Islamic lands)
entries.summary: Explains that Jinn is a Free Virtue marking spirits associated with the Islamic lands, who may belong to the Magic, Faerie or Infernal realm and are vulnerable to Sahir magic.
quotes: The Free Virtue Jinn marks out a category of spirits associated with the Islamic lands.

related.text: The Cradle and the Crescent, Chapters 3 and 4

versions.title: The Jinn
versions.summary: Describes jinn as spirits of place with a spiritual and a material form, the three kinds of jinn by realm, their typical Might, and their regeneration and Virtues.
quotes: typically Mights range from 5–40
related: Realms of Power: The Divine ch.5 Mythic Islam

entries.title: New Virtues for Beasts (Ferocity)
entries.summary: Beasts with Ferocity get a pool of Confidence points usable only when their natural ferocity is triggered, such as defending a den or fighting a natural enemy.
quotes: take three points for you to use when those circumstances are met

entries.title: The Dihi (detachable-head race)
entries.requires: Dihi heritage (Blemmya and human offspring from northern Atbai)
entries.summary: Rules for playing a Dihi, whose head detaches under shock or strain: the stress-die trigger, botch effects, reattaching the head, inheritance, and the Flaw and Virtue that suit the condition.
quotes: Under situations of physical or emotional stress roll a stress die; if the result is 9 or more then her head detaches.
It takes a round to reattach the head to the body.

entries.title: Serpent-dryad growth
entries.requires: Dragon tree grown from Ladon's blood
entries.summary: Describes how dragon trees grown from Ladon's blood produce serpent-dryads and the progression by which the serpent gains heads and improves its Might, Soak, Size, Strength, Confidence and mental Characteristics as the tree flowers.
quotes: At each flowering, the serpent gains an extra head.
For every five heads, the creature gains a point of Might and Soak.

entries.title: Souls in Purgatory and Paradise
entries.requires: Regio of Purgatory or the Earthly Paradise
entries.summary: Rules for statting human souls found in Purgatory and the Earthly Paradise, including their Might Score, capped Abilities, lack of Decrepitude and Warping, and what happens if a soul is retrieved.
quotes: Most souls have a Might of 5.
Add five Might for every point of the character's Confidence Score.
When used, the Abilities of Souls are limited to half of their Might score, rounded up.

entries.title: Mouse Swarm Attacks (Mäuseturm)
entries.summary: A swarm of demonic mice automatically damages victims each round according to the protection they wear, with no attack roll, and is driven off when over half the mice are killed. Includes how area spells and Brawl attacks affect a swarm and why the swarm regenerates in an Infernal aura.
quotes: No attack roll is required for the mice

entries.title: Pomeranian werewolves (skinchanger families)
entries.requires: Born into a Pomeranian werewolf family (storyguide approval)
entries.summary: Explains how shapeshifting is inherited in Pomeranian werewolf families, which Virtue or Flaw a child receives, how animals react to them, and offers a list of suitable additional Virtues and Flaws for playing a werewolf companion.
quotes: A child born into a werewolf family will acquire the Skinchanger Virtue.
Those unlucky enough to be born into human families will usually acquire the Lycanthrope Flaw, and be unable to control their change.
